doc: Increased susceptibility to infections as manifested by repeated bouts of infection.

A mode of inheritance that is observed for traits related to a gene encoded on one of the autosomes in which a trait manifests in individuals with two pathogenic alleles, either homozygotes or compound heterozygotes .
Forceful ejection of the contents of the stomach through the mouth by means of a series of involuntary spasmic contractions.
[MASK] refers to a child whose physical growth is substantially below the norm.

An atrial arrhythmia characterized by disorganized atrial activity without discrete P waves on the surface EKG, but instead by an undulating baseline or more sharply circumscribed atrial deflections of varying amplitude an frequency ranging from 350 to 600 per minute.
An increased susceptibility to bronchitis as manifested by a history of [MASK].
The presence of an abscess located around the anus.
Prolonged and excessive menses at regular intervals in excess of 80 mL or lasting longer than 7 days.

An ecchymosis refers to the skin discoloration caused by the escape of blood into the tissues from ruptured blood vessels. This term refers to an abnormally increased susceptibility to bruising. The corresponding phenotypic abnormality is generally elicited on medical history as a report of frequent ecchymoses or bruising without adequate trauma.

Increased time to coagulation in the partial thromboplastin time test, a measure of the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. Phospholipid, and activator, and calcium are mixed into an anticoagulated plasma sample, and the time is measured until a thrombus forms.
A state of sudden and severe confusion.
Onset of disease at the age of between 16 and 40 years.
Peripheral neuropathy affecting the sensory nerves.
A type of adult onset with onset of symptoms at the age of 40 to 60 years.
A diminution of the volumetric fraction of blood pumped out of the ventricle with each cardiac cycle.
The LV end-diastolic internal diameter was measured from two-dimensional images in the parasternal long-axis view, timed with mitral valve closure at the level of the mitral valve chordae.
Movement-based tics affecting discrete muscle groups.
A developmental defect in which a kidney is located in an abnormal anatomic position.
A condition in which the stomach contents leak backwards from the stomach into the esophagus through the lower esophageal sphincter.
Slow or limited growth after birth.

In utero, the [MASK] serves to divert ventricular output away from the lungs and toward the placenta by connecting the main pulmonary artery to the descending aorta. A patent [MASK] in the first 3 days of life is a physiologic shunt in healthy term and preterm newborn infants, and normally is substantially closed within about 24 hours after bith and completely closed after about three weeks. Failure of physiologcal closure is referred to a persistent or patent [MASK] . Depending on the degree of left-to-right shunting, [MASK] can have clinical consequences.
[MASK] is a developmental defect of the palate resulting from a failure of fusion of the palatine processes and manifesting as a separation of the roof of the mouth .
An abnormality of vibrational conductance of sound to the inner ear leading to impairment of sensory perception of sound.

Distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border more than 2 SD above the mean. Alternatively, an apparently increased distance between nasal base and midline upper lip vermilion border.

The rib cage has the shape of a wide mouthed bell. That is, the superior portion of the rib cage is constricted, followed by a convex region, and the inferior portion of the rib cage expands again to have a large diameter.
A hole between the two bottom chambers of the heart. The defect is centered around the most superior aspect of the ventricular septum.
Radiolucent focal defect of the posterior portion of a rib shaft. The 'gaps' may lead to flail chest.
The presence of an abnormal lateral curvature of the spine.
A fluid filled sac in the kidney.
[MASK] is a congenital abnormality of the interatrial septum that enables blood flow between the left and right atria via the interatrial septum.
Respiratory difficulty as newborn.
Diffuse thickening of the ventricular endocardium and by associated myocardial dysfunction
Episodes of atrial fibrillation that typically last for several hours up to one day and terminate spontaneously.
Short fourth metacarpal bone.

Abnormally small dimension of the Maxilla. Usually creating a malocclusion or malalignment between the upper and lower teeth or resulting in a deficient amount of projection of the base of the nose and lower midface region.

Dental [MASK] refers to an abnormality of the occlusion, or alignment, of the teeth and the way the upper and lower teeth fit together, resulting in overcrowding of teeth or in abnormal bite patterns.
A cutaneous indentation resulting from tethering of the skin to underlying structures of the intergluteal cleft.
Protrusion of the contents of the abdominal cavity through the inguinal canal.
Underdevelopment of the external ear.
Absence or failure to form of the external auditory canal.
A deficiency or slowing down of growth pre- and postnatally.

A [MASK] is an opacity or clouding that develops in the lens nucleus. That is, a [MASK] is one that is located in the center of the lens. The nucleus tends to darken changing from clear to yellow and sometimes brown.
A congenital abnormality of the cornea in which the cornea and the anterior segment of the eye are smaller than normal. The horizontal diameter of the cornea does not reach 10 mm even in adulthood.
A type of cataract affecting the posterior pole of lens immediately adjacent to the Lens capsule.
A reduction of skin color related to a decrease in melanin production and deposition.
Body temperature elevated above the normal range.
A motor disorder characterized by a velocity-dependent increase in tonic stretch reflexes with increased muscle tone, exaggerated tendon reflexes.
A reduction from normal of the mean corpuscular volume, or mean cell volume of red blood cells .
Abnormally increased size of the liver.
Increased concentration of ferritin in the blood circulation.
[MASK] are hyperpigmented lesions that can vary in color from light brown to dark brown with smooth borders and having a size of 1.5 cm or more in adults and 0.5 cm or more in children.
A qualitative impression that red blood cells have less color than normal when examined under a microscope, usually related to a reduced amount of hemoglobin in the red blood cells.
[MASK] results from a defect in the incorporation of iron into the heme molecule. A sideroblast is an erythroblast that has stainable deposits of iron in cytoplasm .
The presence of abnormally shaped erythrocytes.
Any anomaly of the pigmentation of the fundus, the posterior part of the eye including the retina and optic nerve.

[MASK] is vision loss to such a degree as to qualify as an additional support need through a significant limitation of visual capability resulting from either disease, trauma, or congenital or degenerative conditions that cannot be corrected by conventional means, such as refractive correction, medication, or surgery.
Lack of sharpness of vision resulting in the inability to see fine detail.
An axonal neuropathy of peripheral sensory nerves.
Functional neurological abnormalities related to dysfunction of the pyramidal tract.
A decreased concentration of protein in the blood.
A functional abnormality of the autonomic nervous system.
Reduced strength of muscles.
Infrequent or difficult evacuation of feces.
An abnormally decreased calcium concentration in the urine.
Abnormally increased production of urine during the night leading to an unusually frequent need to urinate.
A condition characterized by intermittent involuntary contraction of muscles related to hypocalcemia or occasionally magnesium deficiency.
A subjective feeling of [MASK] characterized by a lack of energy and motivation.
An increased level of renin in the blood.
Increased time between the start of the Q wave and the end of the T wave as measured by the electrocardiogram .
Passing the age when puberty normally occurs with no physical or hormonal signs of the onset of puberty.
An increased rate of urine production.

Inflammation of the tonsils that has occurred repeatedly. The definition of recurrent may vary somewhat, but the criteria used recently as a measure of severity were five or more episodes of true tonsillitis per year, symptoms recurring for at least a year, and episodes that are disabling and that prevent normal functioning. In some cases [MASK] may be related to immunosusceptibility. Evidence exists for a genetic predisposition for [MASK].
Impaired ability to absorb one or more nutrients from the intestine.
Width of the forehead or distance between the frontotemporales is more than two standard deviations above the mean ; or apparently increased distance between the two sides of the forehead.

A [MASK] is a fixed false belief held despite evidence to the contrary. The term [MASK] broadly encompasses all false judgments that possess the following external characteristics to a significant, albeit unspecified, extent: they are held with an exceptional level of conviction, accompanied by an unparalleled subjective certainty; there is an inability to consider alternative experiences or compelling counter-arguments; the content of the belief is impossible.
Changes in one's level of awareness and responsiveness to their environment.
A severe degree of short stature, more than -4 SD from the mean corrected for age and sex.
A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short trunk but a average-sized limbs.
A developmental defect leading to the union of two adjacent vertebrae.

A butterfly vertebra is a sagittal defect in the vertebral body caused by failure of fusion of the two lateral chondrification centers during embryogenesis. The name is based on the appearance of the two hemivertebrae emerging as butterfly wings from the central cleft on x-ray.
Meeting of the medial eyebrows in the midline.

A type of Chiari malformation that consists of brainstem herniation and a towering cerebellum in addition to the herniated cerebellar tonsils and vermis due to an open distal spinal dysraphism/myelomeningocele.
A left-right reversal of the anatomical location of the major thoracic and abdominal organs.
Reduced inferior to superior extent of the thorax.
An abnormal reduction in the amount of air a person can forcefully expel in one second.

A type of bladder dysfunction caused by neurologic damage. [MASK] can be flaccid or spastic. Common manifestatios of [MASK] are overflow incontinence, frequency, urgency, urge incontinence, and retention.
Difficulty in swallowing.

A disorder of the brain caused by an infectious agent that presents with fever, headache, and an altered level of consciousness. There may also be focal or multifocal neurologic deficits, and focal or generalized seizure activity.
An area of depressed vision located at the point of fixation and that interferes with central vision.
An abnormally high concentration in the circulation of alanine aminotransferase .
An increased amount of bilirubin in the blood.
Bilateral bulging of the lateral frontal bone prominences with relative sparing of the midline.

[MASK], also known as [MASK], is an uncommon condition in infants characterized by abnormal thickening of the pylorus muscles in the stomach leading to gastric outlet obstruction. Clinically infants are well at birth. Then, at 3 to 6 weeks of age, the infants present with projectile vomiting, potentially leading to dehydration and weight loss.
A notch or cleft of the retina.

A disordered proliferation of mature tissues that is native to the site of origin, e.g., exostoses, nevi and soft tissue hamartomas. Although most hamartomas are benign, some histologic subtypes, e.g., neuromuscular [MASK], may proliferate aggressively such as mesenchymal cystic [MASK], Sclerosing epithelial [MASK], Sclerosing metanephric [MASK].
Partial or complete wasting of the skin.
Reduced superior to inferior length of the nasal septum.
Hair on the neck extends more inferiorly than usual.
A larger than usual distance between the left and right nipple.
A condition in which the helix is folded over to a greater degree than normal. That is, excessive curling of the helix edge, whereby the free edge is parallel to the plane of the ear.
Depression located on the vermilion of the lower lip, usually paramedian.
The presence of a forehead that is abnormally small.
Congenital developmental defect arising from the primitive branchial apparatus.
An abnormality of refraction characterized by the ability to see objects nearby clearly, while objects in the distance appear blurry.
Agenesis, that is, failure of the kidney to develop during embryogenesis and development.
A congenital anomaly of the urinary tract, in which the kidney is duplicated and is drained via two separate renal pelves and ureters.
A sinus in the coccygeal region . A [MASK] often contains hair and skin debris.
[MASK] is a form of eczema which is closely related to dandruff. It causes dry or greasy peeling of the scalp, eyebrows, and face, and sometimes trunk.

A reduction in the level of performance of the kidneys in areas of function comprising the concentration of urine, removal of wastes, the maintenance of electrolyte balance, homeostasis of blood pressure, and calcium metabolism.
A form of esotropia associated with activation of the accommodative reflex.
A hernia which occurs just below the inguinal ligament, where abdominal contents pass through a naturally occurring weakness called the femoral canal.
A congenital anomaly in which a part or the whole of the cornea acquires the characteristics of sclera, resulting in clouding of the cornea.
Underdevelopment of the thymus.
The presence of one or more cysts of the ovary.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the kidney.
An abnormally decreased concentration of parathyroid hormone.
[MASK] is characterized by increased responsiveness of the tracheobronchial tree to multiple stimuli, leading to narrowing of the air passages with resultant dyspnea, cough, and wheezing.
Anteriorly-facing nostrils viewed with the head in the Frankfurt horizontal and the eyes of the observer level with the eyes of the subject. This gives the appearance of an [MASK] .

A [MASK] is a bent joint that cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement of joints.
Decreased length of the umbilical cord.
Pregnancy-induced hypertension in association with significant amounts of protein in the urine.
An abnormality in which the nuclei of sarcomeres take on an abnormally central localization .
An abnormally high degree of muscle fiber size variation. This phenotypic feature can be observed upon muscle biopsy.
Increased count of eosinophils in the blood.
A type of decreased nerve conduction velocity that affects the motor neuron.

An inflammatory exfoliative dermatosis involving nearly all of the surface of the skin. [MASK] develops suddenly. A patchy erythema may generalize and spread to affect most of the skin. Scaling may appear in 2-6 days and be accompanied by hot, red, dry skin, malaise, and fever.

[MASK] is a malformation of cortical development with abnormally wide gyri with sulci 1,5-3 cm apart and abnormally thick cortex measuring more than 5 mm . See also neuropathological definitions for 2-, 3-, and 4-layered lissencephaly.
Lack of any response to stimulation upon electroretinography.
An abnormal configuration of the lower lip such that it is turned outward i.e., everted, with the Inner aspect of the lower lip vermilion being visible in a frontal view.
[MASK] refers loss of retinal ganglion cells in a characteristic pattern of optic neuropathy usually associated with increased intraocular pressure.
[MASK] is a congenital malformation of the cerebral cortex characterized by abnormal cortical layering and an excessive number of small gyri .

An abnormal appearance of muscle fibers observed on muscle biopsy. Ragged red fibers can be visualized with Gomori trichrome staining as irregular and intensely red subsarcolemmal zones, whereas the normal myofibrils are green. The margins of affect fibers appear red and ragged. The ragged-red is due to the accumulation of abnormal mitochondria below the plasma membrane of the muscle fiber, leading to the appearance of a red rim and speckled sarcoplasm.

A tendency to fall or the inability to keep oneself from falling; [MASK]. The retropulsion test is widely regarded as the gold standard to evaluate [MASK], Use of the retropulsion test includes a rapid balance perturbation in the backward direction, and the number of balance correcting steps is used to rate the degree of [MASK]. Healthy subjects correct such perturbations with either one or two large steps, or without taking any steps, hinging rapidly at the hips while swinging the arms forward as a counterweight. In patients with [MASK], balance correcting steps are often too small, forcing patients to take more than two steps. Taking three or more steps is generally considered to be abnormal, and taking more than five steps is regarded as being clearly abnormal. Markedly affected patients continue to step backward without ever regaining their balance and must be caught by the examiner . Even more severely affected patients fail to correct entirely, and fall backward like a pushed toy soldier, without taking any corrective steps.
Increased levels of protein in the urine.
An unintentional, oscillating to-and-fro muscle movement about a joint axis.
[MASK] is increased hair growth that is abnormal in quantity or location.
A darkening of the skin related to an increase in melanin production and deposition.

An addictive behavior is defined as drinking excessive amounts of alcohol over a prolonged period of time, having difficulty in reducing the amount of alcohol consumed, strongly desiring alcohol, and experiencing withdrawal symptoms when not drinking alcohol.

A febrile seizure is any type of seizure occurring with fever but in the absence of central nervous system infection, severe metabolic disturbance or other alternative precipitant in children between the ages of 3 months and 6 years.

[MASK] is characterized by the presence of a bluish purple, mottled or netlike pattern in unbroken circles on the skin. Exposure to cold environments usually intensifies the vascular pattern. Presumably, the condition results from slow or stagnant blood flow, vessel-wall pathology, and decreased oxygen tension.

A reticular discoloration of the skin with cyanotic areas surrounding pale central areas due to dilation of capillary blood vessels and stagnation of blood within the vessels. [MASK] generally occurs on the legs, arms and trunk and is often more severe in cold weather.

The feeling and belief that one is being targeted or is a focus of negative or untoward actions, overt or covert, from others. The affected individual expresses a concern that people are in general against the individual and are engaging in subtle behaviors to make things difficult for them. The origins of such thinking may arise from real events and become amplified over time. [MASK] may also arise in the absence of any action or interaction between the person and their environment.
An [MASK].
[MASK] is characterized by reduced function of the gonads and results from the absence of the gonadal stimulating pituitary hormones: follicle stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone .
Involuntary movements of one hand that accompany and mirror intentional movements of the opposite hand.
A small elevation of the skin containing cloudy or purulent material usually consisting of necrotic inflammatory cells.
Passage of many stools containing blood.
Inflammation of the lining of the upper small intestine .

The nail disease [MASK] is an often-tender bacterial or fungal hand infection or foot infection where the nail and skin meet at the side or the base of a finger or toenail. The infection can start suddenly or gradually .
Disproportionate shortening of the proximal segment of limbs .
A type of disproportionate short stature characterized by a short limbs but an average-sized trunk.
A developmental anomaly characterized by the presence of two, instead of one, ureter connecting a kidney to the bladder.
A toe that appears disproportionately short compared to the foot.
The presence of a [MASK], related to a duplication of the gallbladder primordium.
Median longitudinal length of the ear more than two standard deviations below the mean in the presence of some, but not all, parts of the normal ear.
Diminished length of a metatarsal bone, with resultant proximal displacement of the associated toe.
Angle formed by the plane of the ear and the mastoid bone greater than the 97th centile for age ; or, outer edge of the helix more than 2 cm from the mastoid at the point of maximum distance .
An abnormality of the biliary tree.
Bleeding from the intestines.
Flat, distinct, discolored area on the lip less than 1 cm wide not associated with a change in the thickness or texture.
An abnormality of the intestine in which part of the intestine invaginates into another part of the intestine.
The presence of a carcinoma of the breast.
Abnormal development of large mammary glands in males resulting in breast enlargement.
Inherited [MASK].
The presence of multiple cysts in both kidneys.
Increased concentration of thyroid-stimulating hormone in the blood circulation.

[MASK] involves all portions of the acinus and secondary pulmonary lobule more or less uniformly. It predominates in the lower lobes and is the form of emphysema associated with1-antitrypsin deficiency. CT scans show a generalized decrease of the lung parenchyma with a decrease in the caliber of blood vessels in the affected lung. Severe [MASK] may coexist and merge with severe centrilobular emphysema. The appearance of feature less decreased attenuation may be indistinguishable from severe constrictive obliterative bronchiolitis.
Extreme dilation of the submucusoal veins in the stomach.

A reduced concentration or activity of circulating alpha-1 antitrypsin, which is a 52-kDa glycoprotein mainly synthesized and secreted by hepatocytes into the bloodstream. Alpha-1 antitrypsin is a serine-proteinase inhibitor that it is crucial in maintaining protease-antiprotease homeostasis in the lungs.
Coughing up of blood or blood-streaked sputum from the larynx, trachea, bronchi, or lungs.
Diffuse enlargement of the entire cerebral hemispheres leading to macrocephaly .
[MASK] is a high pitched sound resulting from turbulent air flow in the upper airway.

[MASK] is a deficiency in voluntary, horizontal, lateral, fast eye movements with retention of slow pursuit movements. The inability to follow objects visually is often compensated by head movements. There may be decreased smooth pursuit, and cancelation of the vestibulo-ocular reflex.

A conenital abnormality of the aortic arch in which the two embryonic aortc arches form a vascular ring that surrounds the trachea or esophagus and then join to form the descending aorta. [MASK] can cause symptoms because of compression of the esophagus or trachea .
A generalized disorder of peripheral nerves.
A dermatosis characterized by thickened, hyperpigmented plaques, typically on the intertriginous surfaces and neck.
A [MASK] is a type of hamartoma that is a circumscribed stable malformation of the skin.
Deeply placed nails.
Rapid and unexpected death.
Excess skin around the neck, often lying in horizontal folds.
The birth of a baby of less than 37 weeks of gestational age.
One or both of the leaflets of the mitral valve bulges back into the left atrium upon contraction of the left ventricle.

Red blood cell distribution width is a simple parameter of the standard full blood count and a measure of heterogeneity in the size of circulating erythrocytes. It is provided by automated hematology analyzers and it reflects the range of the red cell size. It is calculated by dividing the standard deviation of erythrocyte volume by the mean corpuscular volume and multiplied by 100 to convert to a percentage.

The prothrombin consumption test measures the formation of intrinsic thromboplastin by determining the residual serum prothrombin after blood clotting is complete. If there is a defect in the process, less prothrombin will be converted to thrombin than normal . This test may be abnormal with conditions including deficiency of factors VIII or IX, with circulating anticoagulants, thrombocytopenia.

[MASK] is an autoimmune condition affecting the small intestine, triggered by the ingestion of gluten, the protein fraction of wheat, barley, and rye. Clinical manifestations of CD are highly variable and include both gastrointestinal and non-gastrointestinal features. The hallmark of CD is an immune-mediated enteropathy. This term is included because the occurrence of CD is seen as a feature of a number of other diseases.
Increased numbers of platelets in the peripheral blood.
An abnormality in which the mandible is mislocalised posteriorly.

Seizures evoked by visual stimuli. This includes clinical seizures induced by strobe lighting, television and other screens, flickering environmental lighting and self-induction by causing a strobe effect.
A type of hearing loss resulting from a combination of conductive hearing impairment and sensorineural hearing impairment.
Synostosis involving one or more bones of the tarsus .
An exaggerated whealing tendency when the skin is stroked, that is, formation of red, itchy bumps and lines on the skin as a result of pressure on the skin .

Vernix caseosa is a physiological, viscous biofilm that is produced by desquamated fetal skin and sebaceous glands covering the fetus at the third trimester in-utero. The substance's gross morphology in post-partum is described by the etymology, as vernix means varnish, and caseosa means cheesy-like matter. This finding refers to an abnormally thick and greasy vernix caseosa-like scale present at birth.
Recurrent episodes of apnea occurring during infancy.
The presence of a stenosis of the aortic valve.
[MASK] is a type of ventriculoarterial connection in which both great vessels arise entirely or predominantly from the right ventricle.

The presence of an aortic valve with two instead of the normal three cusps . Bicuspid aortic valvue is a malformation of a commissure and the adjacent parts of the two corresponding cusps forming a raphe .
Deposition of calcium salts in the aortic valve.

Diffuse filling of the distal airspaces of the lungs, the alveoli, with macrophages. [MASK] is characterized additionally by thickened alveolar septa and by a sparse inflammatory infiltrate that often includes plasma cells and occasional eosinophils. The alveoli are lined by plump cuboidal pneumocytes. Lymphoid aggregates may be present.
Presence of thickening of the interlobular septa of the lungs as seen on a CT scan.
Supernumerary digits located at the ulnar side of the hand .
Perceived difficulty to breathe that occurs with exercise or exertion and improves with rest.
The presence of blood in the urine. [MASK] may be gross [MASK] or microscopic [MASK] .
An abnormally decreased phosphate concentration in the blood.
Excess facial hair.
Increased width of the skin of vermilion border region of upper lip.

[MASK] refers to delays in the maturation of the brain and central nervous system; infants and young children with [MASK] may experience delays in the development of one or more skills including gross motor abilities, fine-motor coordination, language abilities and ability to solve increasingly complex problems.
Increased width of the skull.

An abnormality of skull shape characterized by a decreased anterior-posterior diameter. That is, a cephalic index greater than 81%. Alternatively, an apparently shortened anteroposterior dimension of the head compared to width.
Absence of the patella.
Duplication of the fibula. This may occur as a part of diplopodia . Diplopodia with double fibula is an extremely rare condition.
Decreased strength of the vocal folds.
An abnormality of refraction characterized by the ability to see objects in the distance clearly, while objects nearby appear blurry.
Increased volume and globular shape of the anteroinferior aspect of the nose.
An increased amount of homogentisic acid in the urine.
An abnormal limitation of knee joint mobility.
An abnormal dark color of the urine.

[MASK] refers to a dimension that is greater than the 95th percentile for the normal person age, sex and body size. In contrast, an aneurysm is defined as a localized dilation of the aorta that is more than 150 percent of predicted . Aneurysm should be distinguished from ectasia, which represents a diffuse dilation of the aorta less than 50 percent of normal aorta diameter.
Abnormal widening of the metaphyseal regions of long bones.

Increased size of the heart, clinically defined as an increased transverse diameter of the cardiac silhouette that is greater than or equal to 50% of the transverse diameter of the chest on a posterior-anterior projection of a chest radiograph or a computed tomography.
[MASK] is a deformity of the hip in which the angle between the femoral shaft and the femoral neck is increased compared to age-adjusted values .
Underdevelopment of the ischiopubic ramus, which is comprised of the inferior pubic ramus and the inferior ramus of the ischium.
A bending or abnormal curvature of the tibia.
Bowing of the femur.
An increased concentration of an amino acid in the urine.
An increased concentration of glucose in the urine.
An increased excretion of phosphates in the urine.
This term describes abnormality of the white matter of the cerebrum resulting from damage to the myelin sheaths of nerve cells.
Underdevelopment of the optic nerve.

[MASK] is the condition of lacking visual perception defined as a profound reduction in visual perception. On the 6m visual acuity scale, [MASK] is defined as less than 3/60. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, [MASK] is defined as less than 20/400. On the decimal visual acuity scale, [MASK] is defined as less than 0.05. [MASK] is typically characterized by a visual field of no greater than 10 degrees in radius around central fixation.
A type of hyperbilirubinemia with neonatal onset.
Disruption of the epithelial layer of the cornea with involvement of the underlying stroma.

A decrease in the ability to perceive vibration. Clinically, this is usually tested with a tuning fork which vibrates at 128 Hz and is applied to bony prominences such as the malleoli at the ankles or the metacarpal-phalangeal joints. There is a slow decay of vibration from the tuning fork. The degree of vibratory sense loss can be crudely estimated by counting the number of seconds that the examiner can perceive the vibration longer than the patient.
Infections of the skin that happen multiple times.
Abnormally [MASK], that is, reduced tear production.
An abnormally decreased level of immunoglobulin E in blood.

[MASK] , also known as the ventricle of Sylvius. The septum pellucidum is a thin, triangular double membrane separating the frontal horns of the right and left lateral ventricles of the brain. It extends between the anterior portion of the corpus callosum, and the body of the fornix and its width varies from 1.5 to 3.0 mm.
Abnormal outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of an artery, vein or the heart.
A reduction in the speed at which electrical signals propagate along the axon of a neuron.
[MASK] is a histologically benign neoplasm located in the ventricular system of the choroid plexus.
A cone-shaped appearance of the epiphyses of the metacarpal bones, producing a 'ball-in-a-socket' appearance. This epiphyses are located at the distal ends of the metacarpal bones.
Increased width of nail.
[MASK] because of underdevelopment of one or more bones of the extremities.
Wide, concave rib end.
Underdevelopment of the ilium ala.
Aplasia of the distal phalanges.
Increased length of the big toe.
A reduced level of insulin-like growth factor 1 in the blood circulation.
An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.
An increase in amplitude of waves returned in ultrasonography of the kidney, which is generally displayed as increased brightness of the signal.
An annular field defect centered on fixation.
A manifest or latent ocular deviation in which one or both eyes tends to deviate temporally.

A [MASK] is an inability to look in a particular direction as a result of cerebral impairment. There is a loss of the voluntary aspect of eye movements, but, as the brainstem is still intact, all the reflex conjugate eye movements are normal.
The presence of six or more cafe-au-lait spots.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the nail.
Abnormal thickening of the skin localized to the palm of the hand and the sole of the foot.
Decreased density/number of eyelashes.
Progressively reduced or lacking hair growth.
Decreased size of the teeth, which can be defined as a mesiodistal tooth diameter more than 2 SD below mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased maximum width of tooth.
[MASK] is a group of conditions in which there is abnormal development of the skin, hair, nails, teeth, or sweat glands.
Any abnormality of the electrical responses of various cell types in the retina as measured by electroretinography.
The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped.
Yellow pigmentation of the skin due to bilirubin, which in turn is the result of increased bilirubin concentration in the bloodstream.
An abnormal flattening of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex I, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.
Reduced ability of the liver to perform its functions.
Increased concentration of ornithine in the blood.
An increased concentration of ammonia in the blood.

Reduced pigmentation of the fundus, typically generalized. Fundoscopy may reveal a low level pigment in both RPE and choroid with clear visibility of choroidal vessels or low pigment level in the RPE with deep pigment in choroid so that visible choroidal vessels are separated by deeply pigmented zones .
Any structural anomaly of the heart and blood vessels.
An abnormality of the fossa cranii posterior , which is made up primarily of the occipital bone and which surrounds to the foramen magnum.
Reduced ability of the lungs to transfer gas from inspired air to the bloodstream as measured by the diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide test.

Swelling of lymph nodes within the mediastinum, the central compartment of the thoracic cavities that contains the heart and the great vessels, the esophagus, and trachea and other structures including lymph nodes.
Subjective feeling of tiredness characterized by a lack of energy and motivation that persists for six months or longer.

Lipofuscin, a generic term applied to autofluorescent lipopigment, is a mixture of protein and lipid that accumulates in most aging cells, particularly those involved in high lipid turnover or phagocytosis of other cell types . This term pertains if there is an increase in the neuronal accumulation of lipofuscin more than expected for the age of the patient.
A neurological condition related to lesions of the basal ganglia leading to typical abnormalities including akinesia , muscular rigidity , chorea , athetosis , and akathisia .

Accumulation of granular osmiophilic material in blood vessel walls. Osmiophilic material becomes black upon staining with osmium tetroxide. Deposition of granular osmiophilic material is the vascular pathological hallmark of CADASIL, which is the most prevalent hereditary small vessel disease and is caused by missense mutations in the NOTCH3 gene. GOM have been shown to contain NOTCH3 ectodomain and extracellular matrix proteins, and can be visualized ultrastructurally in the tunica media of small arteries and capillaries. These electron dense GOM deposits are located in the basement membrane of mural cells, i.e. vascular smooth muscle cells and pericytes. In both manifest and pre-manifest CADASIL patients, GOM deposits are present not only in brain vessels, but also in vessels of other organs, such as the skin.
A type of myoclonus that is induced by voluntary movement. It is made worse by attempts at precise or coordinated movement and may also be provoked by certain sensory stimuli.
A type of encephalocele in the occipital region of the skull. [MASK] presents as a midline swelling over the occipital bone. It is usually covered with normal full-thickness scalp.
An abnormal morphology of the face or its components.
An increased susceptibility to candida infections, as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of candida infections.
Concentration or activity of alkaline phosphatase outside the upper or lower limtis of normal in the blood circulation.
An decreased concentration of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
Reduced ability to perceive painful stimuli.
A type of repetitive behavior in which the affected individual repeatedly waves the hands and/or arms rhythmically.
Hyperconvexity of the thoracolumbar spine producing a rounded or humped appearance.
[MASK] is the focal proliferation of glial cells in the central nervous system.
The presence of atrophy of the corpus callosum.
An abnormal difference between the left and right sides of the face.

Abnormal function of the renal tubule. The basic functional unit of the kidney, the nephron, consists of a renal corpuscle attached to a renal tubule, with roughly 0.8 to 1.5 nephrons per adult kidney. The functions of the renal tubule include reabsorption of water, electrolytes, glucose, and amino acids and secretion of substances such as uric acid.
[MASK] is defined by 3 markers: prominent left ventricular trabeculae, deep intertrabecular recesses, and the thin compacted layer.
Increased volume of the earlobe, that is, abnormally [MASK].
A mild degree of short stature, more than -2 SD but not more than -3 SD from mean corrected for age and sex.
An elevated concentration of luteinizing hormone in the blood.
Absence of both testes from the scrotum owing to failure of the testis or testes to descend through the inguinal canal to the scrotum.
Hypoplasia of the fifth finger, also known as the little finger.
Delayed myelination in the central nervous system.
Punched out lesions in the pigmented layer of the retina.

Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as acute if there is onset of encephalopathy within 8 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.
An abnormal shift in patterns of thinking, acting, or feeling.
Decreased concentration of ceruloplasmin in the blood.

Degeneration of articular cartilage, i.e., of the joint surface. Joint degeneration may be accompanied by osteophytes , narrowing of the joint space, regions of sclerosis at the joint surface, or joint deformity.
A condition caused by a deficiency of parathyroid hormone characterized by hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia.
Death during adolescence, the period between childhood and adulthood .
Absence or underdevelopment of tissue in the central nervous system.
Loose, [MASK].

Proximal interphalangeal flexion deformity of the little finger. That is, the PIP joint of a little finger is bent and cannot be straightened actively or passively. It is thus a chronic loss of joint motion due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.
Involuntary contractions of the neck musculature resulting in an abnormal posture of or abnormal movements of the head.
Involuntary protrusions, movements, spams and contortions of the tongue.
Abnormal development of the anterior segment of the eye globe. These structures are mainly of mesenchymal origin.
The presence of multiple [MASK].

There is inconclusive evidence to precisely define the duration of the seizure; however, based on current evidence an operational threshold of 10 minutes is appropriate as beyond this a seizure is likely to be more prolonged. The individual may or may not be aware or in coma.
EEG with generalized sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec.
A [MASK] is a type of motor seizure characterized by unilateral or bilateral limb stiffening or elevation, often with neck stiffening.
A severe form of hypermetropia with over +5.00 diopters.
Rhythmic, involuntary sinusoidal oscillations of one or both eyes. The waveform of [MASK] may occur in any direction.
A type of congenital cataract in which the opacity follows the anterior or posterior Y suture.
The concentration of ethylmalonic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Repeated transient episodes of metabolic acidosis, that is, of the buildup of acid or depletion of base due to accumulation of metabolic acids.
Paralysis of the external ocular muscles.
Width of the palate more than 2 SD below the mean or apparently [MASK] .
Missing ulna bone associated with congenital failure of development.
Median longitudinal ear length greater than two SD above the mean determined by the maximal distance from the superior aspect to the inferior aspect of the external ear.
An abnormal irregularity of cortical bone.
[MASK] deformity.
The presence of extra bones within a cranial suture. [MASK] are irregular isolated bones which appear in addition to the usual centers of ossification of the cranium.
Abnormal formation of the keratinocytes of the epidermis characterized by persistence of nuclei, incomplete formation of keratin, and moistness and swelling of the keratinocytes.
Decreased number of hairs per unit area of skin of the scalp.
Concentration of protoporphyrins in erythrocytes above the upper limit of normal.
An organ or organ-system abnormality that consists of uncontrolled autonomous cell-proliferation which can occur in any part of the body as a benign or malignant [MASK] .
A tumor that develops in the retrostyloid compartment of the parapharyngeal space, arising from an island of paraganglion tissue derived from the neural crest that is located on the vagus nerve.

A Hoffmann test is performed by flicking the fingernail of the long finger, from dorsal to volar, on each hand while the hand was supported by the examiner's hand. The test was done with the neck in the neutral position and then with the neck maximally forward flexed. Any flexion of the ipsilateral thumb and/or index finger was interpreted as a positive test.
Abnormal function of a sphincter of the urinary bladder.
Small nodular masses which originate in the subependymal region of the lateral ventricles and protrude into the ventricular cavity. They may represent subependymal hamartomas of tuberous sclerosis.
The presence of calcium deposition within the cerebrum.
Areas of the retina lacking pigmentation. [MASK] less than 1 disk diameter in size and tending to be located in the midperiphery of the retina.
A benign tumor of cardiac striated muscle.
Slightly elevated lesions on or in the skin with a diameter of over 5 mm.
A disorder of the cardiac conduction system of the heart characterized by ventricular preexcitation due to the presence of an abnormal accessory atrioventricular electrical conduction pathway.
A delay in the acquisition of the ability to use language to communicate needs, wishes, or thoughts.
A defect in the understanding of complex motor commands and in the execution of certain learned movements, i.e., deficits in the cognitive components of learned movements.
Weakness or partial paralysis in the lower limbs.
Progressive loss of neural cells and tissue.
Progressive deterioration of peripheral axons.
An abnormally increased rate of skeletal maturation. [MASK] can be diagnosed on the basis of an estimation of the bone age from radiographs of specific bones in the human body.
[MASK] is a congenital abnormality of the laryngeal cartilage in which the cartilage is floppy and prolapses over the larynx during inspiration.
An abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
The presence of a mild form of hearing impairment.
A reduction in the freedom of movement of one or more joints.
Abnormally broad metacarpal bones.
Underdeveloped scapula.
A type of cleft lip presenting as a midline gap in the upper lip.
A midline anterior incomplete closure of the abdominal wall in which there is herniation of the abdominal viscera into the base of the abdominal cord.

A genital phenotype that is not clearly assignable to a single gender. [MASK] can be evaluated using the Prader scale: Prader 0: Normal female external genitalia. Prader 1: Female external genitalia with clitoromegaly. Prader 2: Clitoromegaly with partial labial fusion forming a funnel-shaped urogenital sinus. Prader 3: Increased phallic enlargement. Complete labioscrotal fusion forming a urogenital sinus with a single opening. Prader 4: Complete scrotal fusion with urogenital opening at the base or on the shaft of the phallus. Prader 5: Normal male external genitalia. The diagnosis of [MASK] is made for Prader 1-4.
Multiple indentations and/or elevations on the edge and/or surface of the tongue producing an irregular surface contour.
Absence of concavity or convexity of the face when viewed in profile.

An abnormality of the intestinal rotation and fixation that normally occurs during the development of the gut. This can lead to volvulus, or twisting of the intestine that causes obstruction and necrosis.
The presence of a [MASK], which is a neoplasm of the kidney that primarily affects children.
The presence of a malformed cochlea.
Onset of disease manifestations before adulthood, defined here as before the age of 16 years, but excluding neonatal or congenital onset.
An increased susceptibility to infections involving both the paranasal sinuses and the lungs, as manifested by a history of [MASK].
Abnormal decrease of absolute number of monocytes in the blood, per microlitre, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.
A compact, organized collection of mature mononuclear phagocytes, which may be but is not necessarily accompanied by accessory features such as necrosis.
Muscular atrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle.
Muscle hypertrophy affecting the calf muscles.
Muscular dystrophy affecting the muscles of the limb girdle .
A type of multifactorial inheritance governed by the simultaneous action of two gene loci.
A bilateral form of agenesis of the kidney.
Underdevelopment of the ureter.
Congenital occlusion of the vagina or adhesion of the walls of the vagina causing occlusion.
Interalar distance more than two standard deviations above the mean for age, i.e., an apparently increased width of the nasal base and alae.
An abnormal distribution of eyebrow hair growth in the medial direction.
Atypically high degree of awkwardness or apprehension experienced when approaching or being approached by others.
Development of the reproductive system is inconsistent with the chromosomal sex.
Hemorrhage occurring within the skull.

[MASK] is characterized by a fall in blood pH due to a reduction of serum bicarbonate concentration. This can occur as a result of either the accumulation of acids or the loss of bicarbonate from the gastrointestinal tract or the kidney . By definition, MA is not due to a respirary cause.

Difficulty to maintain correct position of the head while standing or sitting. [MASK] is observed when the head seems to flop around or lags posteriorly behind the trunk. Several articles have maintained that head lag should be absent by age 3 to 4 months.
A reduction in the activity of the mitochondrial respiratory chain complex IV, which is part of the electron transport chain in mitochondria.

A limitation in the passive range of motion of the elbow resulting from loss of elasticity in the periarticular tissues owing to structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules or skin.
Failure of the tricuspid valve to close sufficiently upon contraction of the right ventricle, causing blood to regurgitate into the right atrium.
A narrowing of the sacrosciatic notch, i.e., the deep indentation in the posterior border of the hip bone at the point of union of the ilium and ischium.
An alteration of the normally smooth contour of the epiphysis leading to an irregular appearance.
[MASK] is an auditory perception that can be described as the experience of sound, in the ear or in the head, in the absence of external acoustic stimulation.
A developmental defect of tooth color.
Distance between the commissures of the mouth more than 2 SD below the mean. Alternatively, an apparently decreased width of the oral aperture .
The progressive development of an abnormally large skull.
The presence of a [MASK], i.e., a benign tumor originating from the dura mater or arachnoid mater.
An enlargement of the thyroid gland.
A malignant neoplasm originating from the surface ovarian epithelium.
The presence of multiple cysts at the border between the renal cortex and medulla.

[MASK] is a type of focal motor status epilepticus characterized by repeated stereotyped simple motor manifestations such as jerks, typically of a limb or the face, recurring every few seconds or minutes for extended periods .

A [MASK] is a type of generalized motor seizure characterized by bilateral limb stiffening or elevation, often with neck stiffening without a subsequent clonic phase. The tonic activity can be a sustained abnormal posture, either in extension or flexion, sometimes accompanied by tremor of the extremities.

The term [MASK] refers to an abnormal variant of hair that is fine, with tightly coiled curls, and often hypopigmented. Optical microscopy may reveal the presence of tight spirals and a clear diameter reduction as compared with normal hair. Electron microscopy may show flat, oval hair shafts with reduced transversal diameter.
An abnormal localized widening of the aortic root.
Abnormal tortuous form of arteries affecting most or all arteries.
Venous or arterial thrombosis of spontaneous nature and which cannot be fully explained by acquired risk .
Nasal ridge curving anteriorly to an imaginary line that connects the nasal root and tip. The nose appears often also prominent, and the columella low.
Enuresis occurring during sleeping hours.
A reduction in the circulating level of luteinizing hormone .
A reduction of the circulating level of follicle-stimulating hormone .
Developmental hypoplasia of the adrenal glands.
Absence of the distal phalanx of the middle finger.
Small, underdeveloped vertebral bodies.
The presence of only one working lower chamber in the heart, usually with a virtual absence of the ventricular septum and usually present in conjunction with double inlet left or right ventricle.

Three ossification sites are present in typical vertebral bodies : a single ossification center in the vertebral body, and one each in the two neural arches. This term applies if there are additional vertebral ossification centers present during the development and maturation of the spine.
A mild form of myopia with up to -3.00 diopters.
A form of polydactyly in which the extra digit or digits are localized on the side of the thumb or great toe.
The presence of a hamartoma of the hypothalamus.
Underdevelopment of the anterior pituitary gland.
A form of sensorineural hearing impairment that affects both ears.
Onset prior to birth but after 8 weeks of embryonic development .
Structural abnormality of the basal ganglia related to defective development.

The passage of blackish, tarry feces associated with gastrointestinal hemorrhage. [MASK] occurs if the blood remains in the colon long enough for it to be broken down by colonic bacteria. One degradation product, hematin, imbues the stool with a blackish color. Thus, [MASK] generally occurs with bleeding from the upper gastrointestinal tract , since the blood usually remains in the gut for a longer period of time than with lower gastrointestinal bleeding.

An abnormality of histiocytes, in which the cells take on a sea blue appearance due to abnormally increased lipid content. Histiocytes are a type of macrophage. Sea-blue histiocytes are typically large macrophages from 20 to 60 micrometers in diameter with a single eccentric nucleus whose cytoplasm if packed with sea-blue or blue-green granules when stained with Wright-Giemsa.
The repetitive production of the same response to different commands.
The concentration of pyruvate in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
A type of hearing impairment caused by an abnormal functionality of the cochlear nerve with congenital onset.
Vestigial vitreous gel occupying the immediate retrolental space and minimal to no discernible gel in the central vitreous cavity, giving the appearance of an empty vitreous cavity.
[MASK] is characterized by bilateral triangular, morphologically right atrial, appendages, both joining the atrial chamber along a broad front with internal terminal crest.
A left-right reversal of the anatomical location of the viscera of the abdomen.

An elevation above the normal concentration of thyroxine in the blood. Thyroxine is the main hormone secreted by the thyroid gland into the blood. It can be converted into the active form triiodothyronine .
A diffuse, non-pitting edema and thickening of the skin usually on the anterior aspect of the lower legs spreading to the dorsum of the feet.
Reduced amount of the thyroid-stimulating hormone , which is produced by the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates the function of the thyroid gland.
An increased concentration of 4-hydroxy-L-proline in the urine.
A type of retinal neovascularization that affects the posterior pole of the retina.
A small reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at least 50 percent, and a mild reduction is defined as 40-49 percent.

A degenerative disease of the brain characterized by the insidious onset of dementia. Impairment of memory, judgment, attention span, and problem solving skills are followed by severe apraxia and a global loss of cognitive abilities. The condition primarily occurs after age 60, and is marked pathologically by severe cortical atrophy and the triad of senile plaques, neurofibrillary tangles, and neuropil threads.
A type of status epilepticus characterized by a prolonged bilateral tonic-clonic seizure, or repeated bilateral tonic-clonic seizures without recovery between.
A fold of skin starting at or just below the medial aspect of the lower lid and arching upward to cover, extend in front of and lateral to the medial canthus.
A malignancy of the parathyroid glands. [MASK] usually secretes parathyroid hormone, leading to hyperparathyroidism.
Weakness of the muscles of the pelvic girdle , that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the pelvis.

The shoulder, or pectoral, girdle is composed of the clavicles and the scapulae. Shoulder-girdle weakness refers to lack of strength of the muscles attaching to these bones, that is, lack of strength of the muscles around the shoulders.
Underdevelopment of the olfactory bulb.

A developmental disorder characterized by the progressive loss of primordial germ cells in the developing ovaries of an embryo, leading to hypoplastic ovaries composed of wavy connective tissue with occasional clumps of granulosa cells, and frequently mesonephric or hilar cells.
Partial duplication of the distal phalanx of the thumb. Depending on the severity, the appearance on x-ray can vary from a notched phalanx to a partially fused appearance of the two bones.
Accumulation of dark, coarsely granular pigment localized in lysosomes of centrilobular hepatocytes.
Chronic hepatitis characterized by parenchymal inflammation with formation of large multinucleated hepatocytes in response to a variety of insults to the liver.
A form of diabetes insipidus caused by failure of the kidneys to respond to vasopressin .
Displacement of the 3rd finger towards the ulnar side .
An abnormality of the T wave on the electrocardiogram, which mainly represents the repolarization of the ventricles.
Carpal bones with irregular or fragmented margins.

[MASK] is also known as congenital adrenal hyperplasia, which results from disorders of steroid hormone production in the adrenal glands leading to a deficiency of cortisol. The pituitary gland reacts by increased secretion of corticotropin, which in turn causes the adrenal glands to overproduce certain intermediary hormones which have testosterone-like effects.
Involuntary contractions of muscle leading to [MASK] of extremities, neck, trunk, or face.
Short third metacarpal bone.
Intermittent clonic or tonic contraction of muscles supplied by facial nerve. Muscles are relaxed in between contractions.
A type of ventricular tachycardia that is characterized by variable QRS complexes within each lead .
Length of penis more than 2 SD below the mean for age accompanied by hypospadias.
Reduced distance from the anterior border of the naris to the subnasale.
Lack of full passive range of motion of the hip joint resulting from structural changes of non-bony tissues, such as muscles, tendons, ligaments, joint capsules and/or skin.
A type of knee joint contracture in which the knee is in a fixed bent configuration such that it cannot be straightened actively or passively.
Detachment of the nail from the nail bed.
The presence of a carcinoma of the thyroid gland.
Telangiectases located near the surface of the skin of the face.
Hemorrhage occurring between the arachnoid mater and the pia mater.
An anomalous configuration of blood vessels that shunts arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the capillaries and that is located in the gastrointestinal tract.
The presence of small dilated blood vessels near the surface of the mucous membranes of the palate.
Telangiectasia of the tongue.

Thickening of the retina that takes place due to accumulation of fluid in the macula as a nonspecific response to blood-retinal barrier breakdown. [MASK] is a common pathological response to a wide variety of ocular insults, most commonly after intraocular surgery or in association with retinal vascular or inflammatory disease.
Changes in alignment of teeth in the dental arch
Bending or curvature of a fifth toe in the tibial direction .
Increased amplitude of the U wave, defined as an amplitude greater than 1-2mm or 25 percent of the height of the T wave.
An abnormality resulting from a lack of intestinal ganglion cells that results in bowel obstruction with enlargement of the colon.
An abnormal position of the hand in which the wrist is bent toward the radius .
The presence of an increased number of freckles, small circular spots on the skin that are darker than the surrounding skin because of deposits of melanin.
A tumor of the skin.
A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid, varying in size from a pinhead to less than 10mm in diameter at the widest point.
Increased mobility of one ore more metacarpophalangeal joint.
A profound form of hearing impairment.
An abnormality of the pigmentation of the skin.
Insufficient production of steroid hormones by the adrenal glands.
A reduction in the size of nerve terminals.
Applies to a disease manifestation that does not increase in scope or severity over the course of time, i.e., that [MASK] with age.
[MASK] involves proliferation of mesenchymal stromal/stem cells and leads to synovial thickening, which can be observed radiographically.
A sensation of stiffness in the joints that occurs following waking up in the morning.
Underdevelopment of the distal portion of the humerus.
An increased concentration of brain natriuretic peptide in the blood circulation.

A large reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle. The normal range in adults is at over 50 percent, and a severe reduction is defined as less than 30 percent.
A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization that originates in the duodenum.
A type of primitive reflex characterized by an involuntary contraction of the mentalis muscle of the chin caused by stimulation of the thenar eminence of the palm.
A reduced amount of fat tissue in the lowest layer of the integument. This feature can be appreciated by a reduced skinfold thickness.

[MASK] or branching is a common finding in human and rat skeletal muscle pathology. [MASK] refers to longitudinal halving of the complete fiber, while branching originates from a regenerating end of a necrotic fiber as invaginations of the sarcolemma. In fiber branching, one end of the fiber remains intact as a single entity, while the other end has several branches.
A ventricular septal defect that is confluent with and involves the membranous septum and is bordered by an atrioventricular valve, not including the type 3 VSDs.
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the thumb to the little finger that extends distally to at least the level of the proximal interphalangeal joints .
Increased width of the nasal ridge.

[MASK] is characterized by recurrent, non-painful, nonerythematous episodes of eyelid edema. It has been divided into hypertrophic and atrophic forms. In the hypertrophic form recurrent edema results in orbital fat herniation through a weakened orbital septum. Most patients who have [MASK] present in an atrophic condition with atrophy of redundant eyelid skin and superior nasal fat pads.

Usually, Lymphoycytes make up less than 15% of all cells found in the bronchoalveloar lavage fluid. This elevated cell proportion can be induced by virus or drugs, or is associated with specific diseases.

Usually, Neutrophils make up less than 3% of all cells found in the broncho-alveloar lavage fluid. In children, standard value of neutrophils is higher depending on their age . This elevated cell proportion is a sign for acute and chronic infections and can be associated to specific diseases.
Consolidation refers to an exudate or other product of disease that replaces alveolar air, rendering the lung solid .

[MASK] is a benign but potentially destructive growth consisting of keratinizing epithelium located in the middle ear and/or mastoid process. In [MASK], a skin cyst grows into the middle ear and mastoid. The cyst is not cancerous but can erode tissue and cause destruction of the ear.

Insufficient responses to growth hormone provocation tests. GH deficiency is defined as a serum peak GH concentration less than 10 ng/mL on provocation with a combination of at least two separate stimulation tests.
The concentration of L-2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
An increase in the level of L-2-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine.
Inability to sweat.
An increased tendency to fractures following trauma, with fractures occurring without pain.
The spontaneous detachment of a digit from the body due to long standing pathology.

The [MASK] are a group of behavioral motor responses which are found in normal early development, are subsequently inhibited, but may be released from inhibition by cerebral, usually frontal, damage. They are thus part of a broader group of reflexes which reflect release phenomena, such as exaggerated stretch reflexes and extensor plantars. They do however involve more complex motor responses than such simple stretch reflexes, and are often a normal feature in the neonate or infant.
A condition in which there is increased production of gastrin by a gastrin-secreting tumor that stimulates the gastric mucosa to maximal activity, with consequent gastrointestinal mucosal ulceration.
An abnormal increase of bone mineral density with generalized involvement of the skeleton.
An eyebrow that extends straight across the brow, without curve.
Clonus is an involuntary tendon reflex that causes repeated flexion and extension of the foot. [MASK] is tested by rapidly flexing the foot upward.
Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths of the white matter of the brain.
Developmental defect resulting in congenital absence of the middle portion of the clavicle.
Decreased strength of the neck musculature.
Absence of melanin pigment in various areas, which is found at birth and is permanent. The lesions are known as leucoderma and are often found on the face, trunk, or limbs.
Abnormal response to arachidonic acid as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of arachidonic acid.
Lack of platelet dense granules, a type of platelet organelles.
Abnormal platelet response to ADP as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of ADP.
Difficulty with discriminating red and green hues.
A short discontinuity of the margin of the lower or upper eyelid.
A decreased concentration of insulin in the blood.
The concentration of proinsulin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
A conduction block of the left branch of the bundle of His. This manifests as a generalized disturbance of QRS morphology on EKG.
Weakness of the muscles of the arms.
An anomaly of visually evoked potentials , which are electrical potentials, initiated by brief visual stimuli, which are recorded from the scalp overlying the visual cortex.

Complete absence of the dynein arms of respiratory motile cilia, that is, absence of the inner and the outer dynein arms, which normally are situated inside and outside of the peripheral microtubules of motile cilia. This feature is usually appreciated by electron microscopy.
The activity or concentration of hyaluronidase in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
The ability of the elbow joint to move beyond its normal range of motion.
Demyelination of peripheral sensory nerves.
Weakness of the muscles of the legs.
Demyelination of peripheral motor nerves.
A persistent abnormal increase in the pitch of the voice for the context or social situation or significantly different from baseline of the individual.

[MASK] is a lethal myeloproliferative disease of young childhood characterized clinically by overproduction of myelomonocytic cells and by the in vitro phenotype of hematopoietic progenitor hypersensitivity to granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor.
Absent 3rd finger.
A rare congenital vascular anomaly that results when the left superior cardinal vein caudal to the innominate vein fails to regress.
Bending of the diaphysis of the ulna.
Absence of the pectoralis major muscle.
Premature development of the breasts.
Presence of myoglobin in the urine.
Absence of tear secretion.
A decreased concentration of arginine in the blood.
A decreased concentration of citrulline in the blood.

Inflammatory changes in the synovial membranes and articular structures with widespread fibrinoid degeneration of the collagen fibers in mesenchymal tissues, as well as atrophy and rarefaction of bony structures.

Inflammation of the flexor digitorum tendon, often associated with the Kanavel signs: finger held in slight flexion, fusiform swelling, tenderness along the flexor tendon sheath, and pain with passive extension of the digit.
The occurrence of an unusually high amount of muscle pain following exercise.
No pericardium around the heart, occurring as a congenital defect, not the result of a surgical pericardectomy.
Congenital absence of the left half of the diaphragm.
Atresia of the biliary tree.

Congenital large depigmented macule of irergular rhomboid shape. [MASK] generally presents with multiple such macules in the affected individual. There may be smaller , discrete, skin-colored and hyperpigmented macules interspersed within the depigmented macules.
Bleeding at irregular intervals.
The presence of multiple deletions of mitochondrial DNA .
An extra or unusual sound heard during a heartbeat caused vibrations resulting from the flow of blood through the heart.
An increased concentration of lactic acid in the urine.
Abnormally increased formation of dense trabecular bone tissue. Despite the increased density of bone tissue, osteopetrotic bones tend to be more fracture-prone than normal.
An abnormality of the cornea characterized by the deposition of calcium in a band across the central cornea, leading to decreased vision, foreign body sensation, and ocular irritation.
[MASK] is a congenital disease manifested by multiple small [MASK].
Paroxysmal chest pain that occurs with exertion or stress and is related to myocardial ischemia.

The middle finger is more than 2 SD above the mean for newborns 27 to 41 weeks EGA or above the 97th centile for children from birth to 16 years of age AND the five digits retain their normal length proportions relative to each other , or, Fingers that appear disproportionately long compared to the palm of the hand.
Excessive bending, twisting, and winding of a cerebral artery.
Unusual interest in sensory aspects of the environment.
[MASK] is an anatomic finding in the brain manifested by occipital horns that are disproportionately enlarged in comparison with other parts of the lateral ventricles.
Increase in size of one or more joints.
Flaring of the epiphysis.
Frontal schisis of vertebral bodies.
A focal cognitive seizure with forced thinking characterized by retained awareness throughout the seizure.
Separation of the umbilical cord occurs at an abnormally late timepoint.
An abnormally [MASK] of bones caused by an abnormal reduction in bone strength that is generally associated with an increased risk of fracture.
Yellowish discoloration of the nails.
Accumulation of excessive amounts of lymphatic fluid in the pleural cavity.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to the eye.
Abnormal twisting of arteries or veins.
Bluish-grey, spongy nodules associated with scars over pressure points and easily traumatized areas like the elbows and knees.

An abnormality of the hand characterized by metacarpophalangeal hyperextension and proximal interphalangeal and distal interphalangeal flexion. The position of the affected hand is said to resemble a claw.
The presence of an abnormally prominent of the crus of the helix. That is, development of the crus helix to the same degree as an average antihelix stem or helix.
A face that is short and narrow.

[MASK] is caused by obstruction of hepatic venous outflow at any level from the small hepatic veins to the junction of the inferior vena cava with the right atrium, 1 and occurs in 1/100,000 of the general population worldwide. The most common presentation is with ascites, but can range from fulminant hepatic failure to asymptomatic forms. Obstruction of hepatic venous outflow is mainly caused by primary intravascular thrombosis, which can occur suddenly or be repeated over time, accompanied by some revascularization, accounting for the variable parenchymal hepatic damage and histologic presentation. [MASK] is thus a disease, but since it occurs as a manifestation of several other diseases, this term is kept for the present for convenience.
An abnormal decreased number of leukocytes in the blood.
A type of dystonia that affects muscles of the arms.
A deficiency in the intake of energy and nutrients.
Decreased strength of the muscle layer of stomach, which leads to a decreased ability to empty the contents of the stomach despite the absence of obstruction.
A complete loss of the ability to perceive vibration.

A benign, well circumscribed sweat gland neoplasm with eccrine or apocrine differentiation. It usually presents as a solitary, dome-shaped papule, nodule, or plaque on acral sites. It is characterized by a proliferation of uniform basaloid cells in the dermis and it is associated with the presence of focal ductal and cystic structures [NCIT:C27273].
Presence of all the normal ear components and the median longitudinal length more than two standard deviations below the mean.
Shortening of the middle parts of the limbs in relation to the upper and terminal segments.

An anomaly of podocyte morphology characterized by the loss of the interdigitating foot process pattern . The term FPE designates the loss of the usual interdigitating pattern of foot processes of neighboring podocytes, leading to relatively broad expanses of podocyte processes covering the glomerular basement membrane . It is widely viewed as a pathological derangement that is associated with leakage of macromolecules such as albumin through the glomerular filtration barrier.
Lymphadenopathy owing to hyperplasia of follicular centers.
The presence of thrombocytopenia in combination with detection of antiplatelet antibodies.
An anomaly of the space between the medial and lateral canthi of the two open eyelids.

According to the definitions of the American and British Thoracic Societies, including pulmonary functional tests, X-rays, and CT scans for items such as fibrosis, bronchiectasis, bullae, emphysema, nodular or lymphomatous abnormalities.
Anomaly of the contour of the Distal epiphysis of femur such that its normally smooth appearance is irregular.
A systemic disease which can present with cutaneous lesions with or without internal involvement. Tumors are caused by Human herpesvirus 8 , also known as [MASK]-associated herpesvirus .
Permanent indentation on the posteromedial aspect of the helix that may be sharply or indistinctly delineated.
Muscular atrophy involving the muscles of the upper limbs.
Infiltration of numerous eosinophils into the squamous epithelium of the esophagus, and layering of eosinophils on the surface layer of the esophagus.
An abnormal lack of stability of the cervical spine.

[MASK] is a saccular [MASK]. DAA can be either congenital or acquired . Although the majority of patients with congenital DAA are asymptomatic and have a benign course, severe complications, such as rupture or thromboembolism, can occur. DAA is likely to emerge in the third trimester from the aortic junction of the DA, extending towards its pulmonary end.
A widening or ballooning of the dural sac surrounding the spinal cord usually at the lumbosacral level.
Underdevelopment of the musculature.

A rash composed of pustular lesions. A pustule is defined as a vesicle or bulla containing purulent material. It varies in size and may occur at different levels within the epidermis: subcorneal, intraepidermal, or basement membrane zones. The pustules may or may not be sterile and are normally filled with neutrophils.
An abnormally increased sodium concentration in the blood.
Cholangitis associated with evident ductal fibrosis that develops as a consequence of long-standing bile duct inflammatory, obstruction, or ischemic injury; it can be obliterative or nonobliterative.
Elevated concentration of homovanillic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid. HVA is a metabolite of dopamine.
A position of the fetus at delivery in which the fetus enters the birth canal with the buttocks or feet first.
An inversion of the T-wave .

[MASK] is a rare malformation that consists of an abnormal midline connection of the cerebral hemispheres in the posterior frontal and parietal regions, with interhemispheric separation of the basal forebrain, anterior frontal lobes, and occipital regions.
A localized defect in the posterior eye wall with protrusion of uveal tissue due to alterations in scleral thickness and structure.
Decreased retinal arteriolar diameters, which may decrease blood flow and slow oxygen delivery to regions of the retina.
Clefting of the upper lip affecting the lateral portions of the upper lip rather than the midline/median region.
Unilateral underdevelopment of the facial tissues, including muscles and bones.

Nontender, round and firm, but slightly compressible, intradermal or subcutaneous cyst measuring 0.5-5 cm in diameter. Epidermal cysts are intradermal or subcutaneous tumors, grow slowly and occur on the face, neck, back and scrotum. They usually appear at or around puberty, and as a rule an affected individual has one solitary or a few cysts.
A kind of nuclear cataract characterized by fiberglasslike or needlelike crystals projecting in different directions, through or close to the axial region of the lens.
A type of nuclear cataract involving congenital dust-like opacity of the embryonal and fetal nucleus.
A type of hyperparathyroidism caused by a primary abnormality of the parathyroid glands . [MASK] is associated with hyercalcemia.

[MASK] are acellular, calcified deposits within the optic nerve head. [MASK] are congenital and developmental anomalies of the optic nerve head, representing hyaline-containing bodies that, over time, appear as elevated, lumpy irregularities on the anterior portion of the optic nerve.
Increased dimension of the sclera in the anterior-posterior axis.
Splitting of the retinal layers in the macula.
Absence of the semicircular canal.
Two sided hypoplasia of the kidney.
A reduction in immunoglobulin levels of the IgG2 subclass in the blood circulation.
The male foreskin cannot be fully retracted from the head of the penis.
Extracellular tissue deposition of fibrils that are composed of fragments of and/or intact serum amyloid A protein, a hepatic acute phase reactant.
Edema affecting the region situated around the orbit of the eye.
A form of amyloidosis that affects the liver.
An anomaly of a glycosylation process, i.e., a process involved in the covalent attachment of a glycosyl residue to a substrate molecule.
Impaired ability to recognize letters or numbers drawn by an examiner's fingertip on the patient's skin .
Increased discharge of mucus from the nose.
Excessive growth of hands and feet . Typical manifestations include shoe size increase, foot enlargement, glove tightness, and hand enlargement.
Abnormal increase in muscle size and mass not due to training.
Increased intensity of the a reflex in the arm.
Visible increase in width of the non-hallux digit without an increase in the dorso-ventral dimension.
[MASK] is an osseous defect of the pars interarticularis, thought to be a developmental or acquired stress fracture secondary to chronic low-grade trauma.
A developmental defect resulting in an obstructing membrane in the posterior male urethra.
A kind of congenital defect of the anterior abdominal wall in which the intestines are evident through the thin, lax, and protruding abdominal wall in affected infants.
Atrophy of the peroneous muscles, peroneus longus , Peroneus brevis .
The chevron sign refers to an inverted V-shape metaphyses. It is most commonly seen in the distal femur and tends to disappear with age.
Arterial inflammation.

Abnormal increase or decrease of total B cells or any deviation of the propoortion of a B cell subtype. B cells are commonly characterized as CD19+ or CD20+ lymphocytes, or their subpopulations, in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group, measured ex vivo.
Anterior and inferior folding of the upper portion of the ear that obliterates triangular fossa and scapha.

[MASK] is a clinically asymptomatic, 2-4 mm, skin-colored, dome-shaped smooth papule.
