It usually arises in the form of multiple lesions in adults in different areas such as the scalp, forehead, face, and neck. According to histology, the lesion is a fibrotic hamartoma characterized by infundibular epithelial proliferation and perifollicular fibrous proliferation.

A small benign fibrovascular tumor of the dermal part of the hair disk. [MASK] is rather simple in appearance and consists of a dome-shaped fibrous tumor with a prominent vascular component that fills the papillary dermis under an atrophic epidermis. As in a normal hair disk, a hair follicle may be present at one edge of the papular lesion.
Pneumothorax occurring without traumatic injury to the chest or lung.

An ichthyosiform abnormality of the skin that presents at birth or shortly thereafter with generalized erythema, blistering, erosions, and peeling. In the subsequent months, erythema and blistering improves but patients go on to develop hyperkeratotic scaling that is especially prominent along the joint flexures, neck, hands and feet.
Decreased concentration of fibrinogen in the blood.
Defect in the epithelium of the esophagus, essentially an open sore in the lining of the esophagus.
A developmental defect resulting in abnormal closure, or atresia of the tubular structure of the jejunum.
An abnormality in voluntary or involuntary eye movements or their control.
Increased thickness of the external ear.
Increased width of the midpoint of the mandible and overlying soft tissue.
An abnormality of the development of the toenails.
Diminution of tendon reflexes, which is an invariable sign of peripheral nerve disease.

An abnormal change in the cells of the inferior portion of the esophagus. The normal squamous epithelium lining of the esophagus is replaced by metaplastic columnar epithelium. Columnar epithelium refers to a cell type that is typically found in more distal parts of the gastrointestinal system.
Separation of the odontoid process from the body of the axis.
Muscular atrophy involving the muscles of the hand.
Increased concentration of total bilirubin in the blood.

A condition in which middle parts of the hands and/or feet are missing giving a cleft appearance. The severity is very variable ranging from slightly hypoplastic 3rd toe/fingers over absent 2nd or 3rd toes/fingers as far as oligo- or monodactyl hands and/or feet.
Any manifestation of a skin disease associated with the production of pus.
Inflammation of the liver due to infection with enterovirus.
A type of autosomal dominant inheritance involving a gene that is imprinted with maternal silencing.
A type of primary immune deficiency that is characterized by a more severe defect in both the T- and B-lymphocyte systems.

An abnormality of the auditory evoked potentials, which are used to trace the signal generated by a sound, from the cochlear nerve, through the lateral lemniscus, to the medial geniculate nucleus, and to the cortex.
A reduction in the degree of glycosylation of alpha-dystroglycan in muscle tissue.

The ilia is round and hypoplastic with a very flat acetabular roof and a very unusual medial projection of bone that is said to resemble the head of a snail. Figure 4 of PMID:3799723 illustrates this feature.
Wide, concave anterior rib end.
Precocious maturation and calcification of any of the tarsal bones, seven bones of the foot comprising the calcaneus, talus, cuboid, navicular, and the cuneiform bones.
An increase in the level of ketone bodies in the blood.
A chronic form of pancreatitis.
[MASK] is an inflammation of the mucous membranes of any of the structures in the mouth.
The presence of xanthomata in the skin of the eyelid.

An absence of the phase of elevated metabolic activity, during which oxygen consumption increases, that occurs in neutrophils, monocytes, and macrophages shortly after phagocytosing material. An enhanced uptake of oxygen leads to the production, by an NADH dependent system, of hydrogen peroxide , superoxide anions and hydroxyl radicals, which play a part in microbiocidal activity.
Bony fusion of the mandibular condyle to the base of the skull, resulting in limitation of jaw opening.

This corneal dystrophy affects the posterior limiting membrane of the cornea and is characterized by polymorphous plaques of calcium deposits in the deep stromal layers of the cornea, and occasionally by vesicular lesions of the endothelium and edema of the deep corneal stroma.
A type of chronic kidney disease with normal or increased glomerular filtration rate .
A lateral bending or abnormal curvature of the femur.
An abnormality of the morphology of the toes, such that the tips of the toes are prominent and bulbous.
The presence of more than the normal number of carpal bones.
A two-part calcaneus, a finding that probably results from delayed coalescence of two primary calcaneal centers of ossification.
Abnormally wide distal phalanx of finger.
Any structural anomaly of the sebaceous glands.
The most dramatic and severe form of hair loss characterized by an absence of hair follicles.
Inability to ingest sufficient quantities of nutrition by mouth or by tube-feeding with the corresponding requirement for intravenous administration of nutrition.
An erosion of the mucous membrane in a portion of the ileum.
An abnormal concentration of sodium.
An increased concentration of glucose in the blood following a meal.
Underdevelopment of the larynx.
The distal and proximal transverse palmar creases are merged into a single transverse palmar crease on both hands.
A type of sacrococcygeal teratoma located anterior to the sacrum and entirely inside the body .
Excessive growth of the calvaria.
Coma induced by low blood sugar.

[MASK] is a rare cutaneous hamartoma that shows differentiation in the connective tissue sheath of hair follicles. It can occur as a solitary papule or as multiple lesions. Histologically, the lesion consists of a concentric arrangement of cellular fibrous tissue around a normal hair follicle.
An [MASK] is an immune response or reaction to substances that are usually not harmful.
Muscular atrophy of distal arm muscles.
A congenital defect characterized by the absence of one or more permanent teeth, including oligodontia, hypodontia, and adontia of the of permanent teeth.
Exaggerated concavity of the anterior or posterior surface of the vertebral body, i.e., the upper and lower vertebral endplates are hollowed inward.
Bending or curvature of a finger toward the ulnar side . The deviation is at the metacarpal-phalangeal joint, and this finding is distinct from clinodactyly.
A reduction in the number of nerve cells in the basal ganglia.

Nuchal edema is considered present in a fetus at gestational week 14 or more if in the midsagittal plane of the neck, there is subcutaneous edema that produces a characteristic tremor on ballotment of the fetal head. This constitutes the severe end of the spectrum of increased nuchal fold thickness, which is defined as soft-tissue thickening of 6 mm or more, seen in the suboccipitobregmatic view of the fetal head. Nuchal edema may be confined to the neck or it may be generalized, as part of hydrops fetalis.
Absence of the distal interphalangeal flexion creases of the fourth finger.
An anomaly of the brainstem.

[MASK] are small, intra-erythrocytic remnants of erythrocyte nuclei. These inclusions are solitary in each erythrocyte and strongly basophilic. These are often confused with overlying platelets, but can be distinguished by the presence of a halo around overlying platelets.
An increased susceptibility to bronchopulmonary infections as manifested by a history of [MASK].
An abnormal increase in the somatosensory central conduction time , which can be measured from the peak of N13 to the peak of N20 or from the onset of N11 to the onset of N20 .
A type of xanthoma characterized by a nodular form. Tuberous xanthomas are firm subcutaneous nodules,whereby the overlying skin can have red or red-yellow color changes.
The presence of xanthomas extensor tendons .
Encephalopathy with onset in the infantile period.

A condition in which the permanent teeth, because of deficiency of growth in the jaw or segment of jaw, assume a path of eruption that intercepts a primary tooth, causes its premature loss and produces a consequent malposition of the permanent tooth.
A type of anemia characterized by an abnormally low concentration of hemoglobin in the erythrocytes.
Thickening of the periosteum of long bone.
The condition of being unable to eat a full meal because of a feeling of fullness , or or feeling very full after eating only a small amount of food.
Abnormally increased gurgling/rumbling sounds made by the movement of fluid and gas in the intestines.
Concentration of thymidine in the blood circulation above the normal range.

A functional rather than mechanical obstruction of the intestines, associated with manifestations that resemble those caused by an intestinal obstruction, including distension, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, constipation or diarrhea, in an individual in whom a mechanical blockage has been excluded.
Activity of thymidine phosphorylase in the tissues below the lower limit of normal. The activity can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes.
A type of abdominal pain characterized by a feeling of contractions and typically fluctuating in intensity.

A deformity of the sella turcica whereby the sella extends further anterior than normal such that the anterior clinoid process appears to overhang it, giving the appearance of the letter J on imaging of the skull.
A characteristic facial appearance with a round facial form, full cheeks, a short nose, and a relatively small chin.
A type of muscle stiffness that occurs following physical exertion.
A deformity of foot and ankle in which the foot is bent down and outwards.

Central nervous system dysfunction in association with liver failure and characterized clinically by lethargy, confusion, nystagmus, decorticate posturing, spasticity, and bilateral Babinski reflexes.
Abnormal response of natural killer cells to stimuli.
An elevation above the normal ratio of blood phytanic acid concentration to pristanic acid concentration.
An chronic form of hemolytic anemia.
An increased amount of unconjugated bilurubin in the blood.
An abnormal localized widening of the thoracic aorta.
An abnormal localized widening of the abdominal aorta.
Failure of growth hormone levels to respond adequately to the insulin tolerance test .
A reduction in the amplitude of sensory nerve action potential in distal nerve segments. This feature is measured by nerve conduction studies.
Uncontrolled episodes of crying occur without any apparent motivating stimuli.
Underdevelopment of the frontal lobe of the cerebrum.
Lack of eyelashes on the lower lid.
An abnormality of coagulation associated with an increased risk of thrombosis.
One or more bent toe joints that cannot be straightened actively or passively.
Concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
An abnormally increased level of immunoglobulin D in blood.

Infiltration of eosinophils in the stomach mucosa, that is diagnosed by an upper endoscopy and microscopy that shows more than 20 eosinophils per high-power field in association with peripheral eosinophilia and the absence of secondary cause of eosinophilia.
Accumulation of pus in the pleural cavity.

Candida infections of the esophagus are considered opportunistic infections and are seen most commonly in immunosuppressed patients, the most common symptoms being dysphagia, odynophagia, and retrosternal pain.
Longitudinal grooves in the surface of the esophagus arranged in a longitudinal fashion .

A [MASK] occurs when a bone breaks in an area that is weakened secondarily to another disease process such as tumor, infection, and certain inherited bone disorders. A [MASK] can occur without a degree of trauma required to cause fracture in healthy bone.
Spoon-shaped, broad thumbs.
Esotropia in which either eye may be used for fixation.
Any morphological abnormality of the skin.
Inflammation of the vitreous body, characterized by the presence of inflammatory cells and protein exudate in the vitreous cavity.
The concentration of delta-1-pyrroline-5-carboxylate in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
Multiple small zones of sarcomeric disorganization and lack of oxidative activity in muscle fibers.
An abnormal vertical orientation of the clivus .
Irregular morphology of one or more metacarpal bones.
A localized myotonic contraction in a muscle in reaction to percussion .
Increased concentration of 4-hydroxyphenylacetic acid in the urine.
The presence of abnormal punctate calcifications in one or more tarsal bones.
Nasal ridge curving posteriorly to an imaginary line that connects the nasal root and tip.
Inflammation of the episclera, a thin layer of tissue covering the white part of the eye.
Partial dislocation of the head of the radius.
Abnormal thickening of of the outer layer of the adrenal gland due to fibrosis.
Decrease in the level of adenosine deaminase , an enzyme involved in purine metabolism, within erythrocytes. ADA is involved in the catabolism of adenosine.
Absence or underdevelopment of the middle phalanx of the little finger.
Any structural anomaly of the heart.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against nuclei or nuclear components.
A type of resting tremor characterized by simultaneous rubbing movements of thumb and index fingers against each other.
A type of dystonia that affects the midline muscles, i.e., the chest, abdominal, and back muscles.
Marked, involuntary jerking of the eyelids.
A type of tremors that is triggered by holding an arm in a fixed position.
A defect in the ability to concentrate the urine.

[MASK] are hyperkeratotic papules that are characterized histologically by superficial ectatic blood vessels with epidermal proliferation. Clinically, [MASK] presents as a small, raised, dark-red spot.

[MASK] is typically characterized by innumerable small red to black papules which occur in clusters and are situated symmetrically in the bathing trunks area. The number of lesions and the extension of the body increase steadily with time so that generalization and mucosal involvement are common. The single lesion begins with a minute reddish papule which enlarges to up to 10 mm in diameter, becomes dark red to black with a discrete keratotic overgrowth. Histologically, the papules are characterized by superficial dilated capillaries in papillary dermis with epidermal proliferation.
An increased lipid content in the urine.

Pilomatricoma is an asymptomatic slowly growing benign cutaneous tumor, differentiating towards the hair matrix of the hair follicle. It is covered by normal or hyperemic skin, and usually varies in size from 0.5 to 3 cm.
A nail plate that has a longitudinal separation and the two sections of the nail share the same lateral radius of curvature.
Abnormal [MASK].
Reduced ability to control, or a failure to resist a temptation, urge, or impulse. Examples include disregard for social conventions, general impulsivity, and poor risk assessment.

Decreased fetal activity associated with multiple joint contractures, facial anomalies and pulmonary hypoplasia. Ultrasound examination may reveal polyhydramnios, ankylosis, scalp edema, and decreased chest movements .
Loss of elasticity of the upper and lower eyelids causing the skin to sag and bulge.

Fusion of cervical vertebrae at C6 and C7, caused by a failure in the normal segmentation or division of the cervical vertebrae during the early weeks of fetal development, leading to a short neck with a low hairline at the back of the head, and restricted mobility of the upper spine.
The absence of one or more teeth from the normal series by a failure to develop
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to the foot.
A collection of pathologic conditions that result from progressive spinal cord dysfunction secondary to cord compression in the cervical spine.
An abnormality of the normal developmental rotation of the kidney leading to an abnormal axial orientation of the kidney.
An [MASK], which is defined as the structures surrounding the shoulder joint where the humerus attaches to the scapula.
Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the forehead.
Underdevelopment of the spleen.

The concentration of type I procollagen aminoterminal propeptide in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. The aminoterminal propeptide of type I procollagen in serum is a sensitive indicator of the synthesis of type I collagen.
Abnormal increase of absolute number of neutrophils in the blood, per microliter, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.
An abnormal narrowing of the lumen of the esophagus.
A medium reduction in the fraction of blood pumped from the left ventricle with each cardiac cycle, defined as a left ventricular ejection fraction of 30-39 percent.
Abnormal narrowing of the coronary artery.
Enlargement of the soft tissues of one or more fingers.
An inability of the tubules in the kidney to reabsorb small molecules, causing increased urinary loss of electrolytes , minerals, glucose, amino acids, and water.

An elevated concentration in the blood of hemoglobin A2 , which is a normal variant of hemoglobin A that consists of two alpha and two delta chains and is normally present at low levels in adults but may be increased in beta thalassemia.
An abnormal dilatation of lymph vessels in the pericardium.

[MASK] is the formation of nodes along the hair shaft through which breakage readily occurs. It is thus a focal defect in the hair fiber that is characterized by thickening or weak points that cause the hair to break off easily. The result is defective, abnormally fragile hair.
An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage, and arises from a bone that develops from cartilage.
Schisis of vertebral bodies.
Tremulousness of the iris on movement of the eye, occurring in subluxation of the lens.

[MASK] is a symptom of peripheral arterial occlusive disease. After having walked over a distance which is individually characteristic, the patients experience pain or cramps in the calves, feet or thighs which typically subsides on standing still.
An abnormality of the gyri of the cerebral cortex of the brain.
The inability to maintain a comfortable body temperature in warm or hot weather.
Activity of the enzyme beta-mannosidase below the lower limit of normal. Beta-mannosidase is a lysosomal enzyme that catabolizes oligosaccharides.
Concentration or activity of beta-mannosidase below the lower limit of normal. Beta-mannosidas enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts.
The presence of an abnormal curvature of the cervical vertebral column.
A thickening of the stratum corneum in the region beneath the nails.
Decreased level of the enzyme gamma-glutamyltransferase . GGT is mainly present in kidney, liver, and pancreatic cells, but small amounts are present in other tissues.
Popcorn calcifications are areas of amorphous calcifications often with rings and arcs that resemble popped corn kernels in the metaphysis and epiphysis around the growth plate.
An increased concentration of chloride in the urine.
An increased concentration of potassium in the urine.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes two to four.
An episodic form of supraventricular tachycardia with abrupt onset and termination.
A deviation from the normal discoid platelet shape.
Nails whose growth is slower than normal.
The concentration of D-gyceric acid in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
A tumor of a salivary gland.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the aorta.
Saccadic undershoot of horizontal saccadic eye movements, i.e., a horizontal saccadic eye movement that has less than the magnitude that would be required to gain fixation of the object.
Acute progressive areflexic weakness and mild sensory changes resulting from myelin breakdown and axonal degeneration.
Enlargement of the diameter of a coronary artery as defined by a focal dilation of a segment at least 1.5 times larger than the reference vessel.
An abnormality of the mitochondria in muscle tissue.
Dislocation of many joints.
[MASK] are tiny yellow or white accumulations of extracellular material that build up in Bruch's membrane of the eye.
[MASK] is the creation of new blood vessels in the choroid layer of the eye.
Chronic reduction in active and passive mobility of the shoulder joint due to structural changes in muscle, tendons, ligaments, or skin that prevents normal movement.

Streaming or smearing of the Z band, which is then no longer confined to a narrow zone which bisects the I band. The Z disk may extend across the I band or the entire sarcomere in a zigzag manner. Focal thickening, smudging, and blurring of the Z band takes place concurrently. Myofibrillar disorganization is a frequent but not invariable accompanying change.
A developmental anomaly characterized by abnormal smallness of both eyes.

A type of astigmatism in which an unequal curvature of the cornea and some cases additionally of the lens causes one meridian of the eye to be hyperopic and a second meridian that is perpendicular to the first to be myopic .

A pathologic entity characterized by a developmental defect in a long bone leading to bending and pathologic fracture, with inability to form a normal bony callus with subsequent fibrous nonunion, leading to the pseudarthrosis .

Hyperphalangy is a digit morphology in which increased numbers of phalanges are arranged linearly within a toe. That is, there is an accessory phalanx that is arranged linearly with the other phalanges.
Mechanical percussion leads to spreading waves of muscle contractions that begin proximally and spread laterally across the muscle.
Loss of bone mass occurring beneath the periosteum . This process may create a serrated and lace-like appearance in periosteal cortical bone.
A visual defect characterized by the inability to see as clearly in bright light as in dim light. The word [MASK] literally means [MASK].
Hypopigmented hair that appears white.
Lack of skin pigmentation .
An elevated level of propionylcarnitine in the circulation. Propionylcarnitine is present in high abundance in the urine of patients with Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase deficiency.
[MASK], which is the largest nucleus of the basal ganglia, comprising the caudate, putamen and ventral striatum, including the nucleus accumbens.
Mottling of the retinal pigment epithelium, i.e., localized or generalized fundal pigment granularity associated with processes at the level of the retinal pigment epithelium.
Dagger-shaped calcifications in the dental pulp.
Thickening and hardening of the epidermis seen with exaggeration of normal skin lines.
The presence of amyloid deposition in the superficial dermis.
Incomplete maturation or aberrant formation of the male gametes.
Reduced level of the compound muscle action potential , which is recorded following electrical stimulation of a nerve from surface electrodes overlying a muscle supplied by that nerve.
A developmental defect resulting in the congenital absence of skin on the trunk or the limbs.
Presence of an unusually high number of lentigines , which are flat, tan to brown oval spots.
The concentration of 3-hydroxyglutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Fibrous band between the mucosal surfaces of the upper and lower alveolar ridges.
A higher than normal levels of the fatty acids which can occur in plasma as a result of lipolysis in adipose tissue or when plasma triacyglycerols are taken into tissues.

[MASK] refers to an abnormally placed and deformed tricuspid valve characterized by apical displacement of the septal and posterior tricuspid valve leaflets, leading to atrialization of the right ventricle with a variable degree of malformation and displacement of the anterior leaflet.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to the jaw.

Abnormal structure of the sperm axonemal structure which consists of a ring of nine microtubular doublets and a central pair of microtubules, giving the classical 9+2 microtubular arrangement. The axoneme contains a central pair of microtubules that are connected by a bridge-like structure forming the central pair complex . Each of the nine outer doublets is composed of type A and B microtubules and connected by radial spokes to the CPC.
An increased amount of subcutaneous fat tissue around the neck.
Fibrous dysplasia of the bones were lesions are localized in many bones throughout of the body. [MASK] is a cardinal feature of McCune-Albright syndrome.
An elevation in bone density in the ilium. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.
Duplicated basement membranes of the peritubular capillaries located in the medulla of the kidney and arranged in multiple concentric layers.

A type of epidermal nevus that appears as skin-colored-to-brown, sharply demarcated, papillomatous papules that coalesce into plaques. The majority of these nevi are either present at birth or occur within the first year of life.
A circumscribed, solid elevation of skin with no visible fluid that is reddish in color.
Underdevelopment of muscles of the arm.
A type of stenosis of the external auditory meatus in which the opening of the external auditory meatus appears as a vertical slit.
Syndactyly with fusion of toes three and four.
An infection of the umbilicus and/or surrounding tissues occurring in the neonatal period.
Head movements associated with nystagmus, that may represent an attempt to compensate for the involuntary eye movements and to improve vision.
The presence of sensorineural deafness with late onset.
Positive result of the 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine urine test, which indicates the presence of alpha-ketoacids in the urine.
Concentration of a branched chain amino acid in the blood above the upper limit of normal.
An increased concentration of dermatan sulfate in the urine.

[MASK] is a congenital eyelid anomaly characterized by horizontal enlargement of the palpebral fissure. The eyelid is shortened vertically compared with the horizontal dimension, with associated lateral canthal malpositioning and lateral ectropion abnormally wide lid opening.
A tumor of the skin or mucous membrane with finger-like projections.
A ratio of serum triiodothyronine to thyroxine in the blood that is higher than normal.
Lack of transparency of the corneal epithelium.
Decreased count of erythroid precursor cells, that is, erythroid lineage cells in the bone marrow.
A nail of the fifth finger that is diminished in length and width, i.e., underdeveloped nail of little finger.
Absence or underdevelopment of the distal phalanges of the toes.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against reticulin.

An abnormality observed by retinal fluorescein angiography, which involves the intravenous injection of fluorescein dye followed by fluorescent imaging of the fundus immediately after injection and for up to ten minutes thereafter. It can be used to study various retinal abnormalities including especially anomalies of the choroidal and retinal circulation.
Bending or curvature of a toe in the tibial direction .
An abnormal reduction in dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase level.
Increased concentration of uracil in the urine.
The presence of developmental dysplasia of the optic nerve.
The presence of an adenoma in the cortex of the kidney.
A benign tumor of the parathyroid gland that can cause hyperparathyroidism.
Underdevelopment of the pharynx.
An increased concentration of the MM isoform of creatine kinase in the blood circulation.
Excessive, increased hair growth located in the elbow region.
A increased anteroposterior thickness of the cornea.
Concentration of the complement component C8 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
Partial dislocation of the radioulnar joint.
Underdevelopment of the second toe.
A reduction in the amount of adipose tissue compared with the amount previously present in an individual.

A condition which is considered to be due to the subsequent atrophy and disappearance in fetal life of an initially normal testis. In the presence of spermatic cord structures is evidence of the presence of the testis in early intrauterine life. When associated with a blind-ending spermatic cord, this entity is named as his absence of a testis in an otherwise normal 46XY male is usually unilateral and is assumed to be a consequence of intrauterine or perinatal torsion or infarction.
A rare birth defect in women where the urethra and vagina both open into a common channel.
Unusual gonadal development in a person with a 46,XY male karyotype, leading to a more female sex differentiation.

Pleomorphic xanthoastrocytomas are rare low-grade astrocytomas typically found in the temporal lobe and classically presenting with epilepsy. PXA is an astrocytic neoplasm that most often presents in children or young adults but can also occur in adults. The diagnosis of anaplastic PXA is made based upon tumor histopathologic characteristics and requires increased proliferative activity , which is associated with worse overall survival. In general, anaplastic PXAs acquire features of a more aggressive astrocytic neoplasm that can include increased proliferation, necrosis, microvascular proliferation, loss of pericellular reticulin, and increased infiltrative growth.
Lack of strength of the proximal musculature occurring late in the clinical course.
Disproportionately short middle and distal phalanges compared to the hand/foot.
A cataract which affects the layer of the lens surrounding the nucleus, i.e., the lens cortex. It is identified by its unique wedge or spoke appearance.
Generalized abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body.
Slender, slit-like aperture of the nostril.
Phocomelia involving all four extremities.

A type of anterior encephalocele in which there is a protrusion of the contents of the skull through a breach at the point where the frontal and ethmoidal bones meet. [MASK] can be divided further into three distinct categories: nasofrontal, nasoethmoidal, and nasoorbital.
Any abnormal shape or structure of the metacarpal bones.
A developmental defect in a the clavicule leading to bending and pathologic fracture, with inability to form a normal bony callus with subsequent fibrous nonunion, leading to the pseudarthrosis .
Reduced bulkiness of the crease or fold of skin running from the lateral margin of the nose, where nasal base meets the skin of the face, to a point just lateral to the corner of the mouth .
Disruptions in the production of speech sounds, with involuntary repetitions of words or parts of words, prolongations of speech sounds, or complete blockage of speech production for several seconds.
Bigonial distance more than 2 standard deviations below the mean ; or an apparently decreased width of the lower jaw when viewed from the front .
Folds or ridges within the concha that are distinct from the crus helix.
A separation of the layers of an artery.
An increased number of mitochondria detected in neutrophils.
Any abnormality in the multiplication or reproduction of B cells, which results in the expansion of a cell population.
Inflammation of the biliary ductal system, affecting the intrahepatic or extrahepatic portions, or both.
Recurrent episodes of oral herpes, typically characterized by blisters or ulcers on the gums, lips and/or tongue caused by herpes virus.
Decreased amount of pigmentation in the macula lutea.
Limbus-to-limbus corneal thinning, often greatest in the periphery, with globular protrusion of the cornea.
An anomalous concentration of testosterone in the blood.

Absence of any measurable level of sperm in his semen, resulting from a defect in the production of spermatozoa in the testes. This can be differentiated from obstructive azoospermia on the basis of testicular biopsy.
Increase in bulk of the ala nasi.
The presence of prolapse of the uterus.
The presence of complement 3 deposits in the glomerulus.

Abnormal increase in blood pressure. An individual measurement of [MASK] does not necessarily imply hypertension. In practical terms, multiple measurements are recommended to diagnose the presence of hypertension.
Inflammation of the sac-like covering around the heart .
An increased susceptibility to Aspergillus infections, as manifested by a history of recurrent episodes of Aspergillus infections.
Peripheral arterial stenosis with onset before the age of 50 years.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of medium-sized arteries.
Calcification, that is, pathological deposition of calcium salts in the tunica media of large arteries.
A neoplasm of the pineal gland.

The feeling of frustration can be defined as an emotional reaction that occurs when a desired goal is not achieved. Frustration intolerance is defined as an age-inappropriate response to frustration, characterized by crying or temper tantrums in children, or aggressive or other maladaptive behaviors.
A [MASK] is a type seizure beginning with a subjective sensation.
Edema/fluid accumulating between the retinal pigment epithelium and Bruch's membrane.
A [MASK] is a type of bilateral tonic-clonic seizure characterized by generalized onset; these seizures rapidly engage networks in both hemispheres at the start of the seizure.
Absence of the sebaceous gland, the holocrine gland that secretes sebum into the hair follicles, or in hairless areas into ducts.
Gout affecting the Metatarsophalangeal joint of big toe.
An abnormally high level of uric acid in the urine.
Description of conditions that are exclusively or predominantly observed to display de novo variants. In some cases, this may be due to the limited reproductive fitness of affected individuals.
A clot that obstructs blood flow in a mesenteric vein .
Absent 4th finger.
Absence of the third long bone of the hand.
Absence of the fourth long bone of the hand.
Developmental hypoplasia of the apocrine sweat glands in the region of the axilla.
Absent 5th finger.
Lack of intentional participation in interactions with another person.
A type of gait ataxia displaying progression of clinical severity.
A decreased amount of glycogen in muscle tissue.

A chronic epithelioid cell granulomatous inflammation of the meibomian gland caused by inflammation of a blocked meibomian gland. A [MASK] or meibomian cyst appears as a painless tuberous swelling in the upper lid without loss of eyelashes.
[MASK] is a condition which occurs in pregnancy when the amniotic sac ruptures more than an hour before the onset of labor.
The amount of N-acetylaspartate in the urine, when corrected for urine concentration, is above upper limit of normal. This feature can be measured using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry.
Recurrent episodes of brain dysfunction that may be triggered by factors such as metabolic disturbances or infections.
A developmental growth retardation of the vertebral end plates that may lead to secondary destruction of the vertebral end plates and protrusion of the nucleus pulposus into the vertebral body .
A small break in the retina.
An increase in the number of chromosome sets per cell in bone marrow cells.
A kind of anemia characterized by inadequate production of erythrocytes.

Concentration or activity of alpha-N-acetylglucosaminidase below the lower limit of normal. This enzyme can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts. It is also known as alpha-acetylglucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-D-glucosaminidase, N-acetyl-alpha-glucosaminidase, and alpha-D-2-acetamido-2-deoxyglucosidase.

A stroke related to a small infarct in the deep cerebral white matter, basal ganglia, or pons, that is presumed to result from the occlusion of a single small perforating artery supplying the subcortical areas of the brain.
Inflammation of the meninges related to infection by Epstein-Barr virus.
The amount of hydroxyphenyllactic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
A disease where there is cellular death of bone components due to interruption of the blood supply.
Decreased intensity of the Achilles reflex , which can be elicited by tapping the tendon is tapped while the foot is dorsiflexed.
A form of sensorineural hearing impairment with onset after the acquisition of speech.
A break or crush injury of the thigh bone .
Position of the liver across the middle of the body instead of being in its normal position to the right of the stomach.
Underdevelopment of the arch of aorta.
The presence of a dilated urinary bladder.
An abnormal widening of the diameter of the pulmonary artery.
Abnormal fat accumulation in the kidneys.
Any anomaly in the process by which myelin sheaths are formed and maintained around neurons.
An increase in the reabsorption of calcium by the renal tubulus that is not associated with increased parathormone levels.
An increased concentration of cystine in the urine.
Absence of the two central microtubules of motile cilia with a 9+2 microtubuluar configuration.
Repetitive and compulsive picking of skin which results in tissue damage.
Absence of the clavicles as a developmental defect.
Lack of formation of mineralized bony tissue of the sternum.
Lack of development of the glenoid fossa, also known as the glenoid cavity, which is the articular surface of the scapula that articulates with the head of the humerus.
A neuropathic disorder characterized by episodes of intense pain in the face, originating from the trigeminal nerve. One, two, or all three branches of the nerve may be affected.

Hermaphroditism refers to a discrepancy between the morphology of the gonads and that of the external genitalia. In [MASK], the genotype is female and the gonads are ovaries, but the external genitalia are virilized.
Passage of excessive amounts of gas and the feeling of abdominal fullness and bloating.
Noticeably unpleasant odors exhaled in breathing.
A type of focal autonomic seizure characterized by symptoms or signs pertaining to the gastrointestinal system as the initial semiological feature.
A type of focal autonomic seizure characterized by changes in heart rate as the initial semiological feature.
A seizure characterized by elementary auditory phenomena including buzzing, ringing, drumming or single tones as its first clinical manifestation.
A focal seizure characterized at onset by coordinated motor activity. This often resembles a voluntary movement and may consist of an inappropriate continuation of preictal motor activity.
Seizures characterized by olfactory phenomena as its first clinical manifestation.
Abnormal number of platelets per volume of blood. In a healthy adult, a normal platelet count is between 150,000 and 450,000 per microliter of blood.
A diminished activity of the classical complement pathway as measured by the assay for 50% haemolytic complement activity of serum.
Concentration of the complement component C5 in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
An abnormality of the conjunctiva.
Abnormal arrangement of the structures of the motile cilium.
Agenesis of one or more central incisors, i.e., of lower secondary incisor, lower primary incisor, upper secondary incisor, or of upper central primary incisor.
The amount of glycolic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
An abnormality of the dermatoglyphs, i.e., an abnormality of the patterns of ridges of the skin of palm of hand.

Chronic loss of joint motion in the 5th finger due to structural changes in non-bony tissue. The term camptodactyly of the 5th finger is used if the distal and/or proximal interphalangeal joints are affected.
Aplasia, that is failure to develop, of the fallopian tube.
A structural anomaly of the external genitalia.
Concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
A reduction in the expression of CD43 on the cell surface of lymphocytes.
Abnormality of left ventricular contraction, often defined operationally as an ejection fraction of less than 40 percent.
Partial dislocation of the lens of the eye.
Absence of the middle phalanx of the little finger.
An abscess not caused by infection with pyogenic bacteria. Operationally, a [MASK] is inferred if investigations of an abscess fail to reveal evidence of pathogenic organisms.
Focal proliferation of glial cells in the substantia nigra.
A type of [MASK] that is characterized by disrupted cortical lamination and specific cytological abnormalities.
Shortening of the middle parts of the arm in relation to the upper and terminal segments.
A flat, distinct, discolored area of skin less than 1 cm wide that does not involve any change in the thickness or texture of the skin.
Absence of urine, clinically classified as below 50ml/day.

Systemic desaturation of a liveborn baby resulting from persistent pulmonary hypertension with a patent ductus arteriosus and patent foramen ovale, such that the circulation in postnatal life follows the fetal course.
The presence of multiple exostoses on the scapula. An exostosis is a benign growth the projects outward from the bone surface. It is capped by cartilage.
A reddish-blue mottled condition of skin caused by inflammation of the cutaneous blood vessels.
An abnormal appearance of hair under polarizing microscopy , whereby hair shafts show striking alternating bright and dark bands, often referred to as [MASK].
An asymmetriy, i.e., difference in size, shape or position between the left and right ear.
Abnormality of the anal canal.
This term groups together three conditions that presumably represent different degrees of severity of a [MASK] or nasal tip.
The presence of a [MASK].

Abnormal arrangement of the structures of the axoneme, which is the cytoskeletal structure that forms the inner core of the motile cilium and displays a canonical 9+2 microtubular pattern of motile cilia studded with dynein arms.
Lack of stability of a distal joint .
A carcinoma that arises in a sebaseous gland

A contracture that limits the ability of the forearm to stabilize the hand in pronation , meaning that the palm is fixed in a upward orientation. Restriction of supination/pronation can occur at the elbow , at the wrist , and anywhere in between.
Dilatation of the vestibule of the inner ear.
Lack of detectible CD8-positive T cells
Bony fusion of the middle and proximal phalanges of the 4th toe.
A structural abnormality of retinal vasculature.
A need to strictly adhere to repetitive routines or patterns of behavior which are created by the environment. One becomes upset or distressed when their routines are disrupted or altered.
Spasticity of one or more muscles innervated by the facial nerve.
A type of conductive deafness with congenital onset.

A myxoma of the heart. Cardiac myxomas consist of stellate to plump, cytologically bland mesenchymal cells set in a myxoid stroma. Cardiac myxomas are of endocardial origin and general project from the endocardium into a cardiac chamber.
The presence of abnormal calcium deposition lesions in the pancreas.
Spontaneous development of hematomas or bruises without significant trauma.
Defective structure and function of myelin sheaths. Dysmyelination is distinguished from demyleination where there is destruction or damage of previously normal myelination.
Abnormal response to collagen-related peptide as manifested by reduced or lacking aggregation of platelets upon addition of CRP.
An abnormally increased amount of 7-biopterin in the urine.

A hazy, grayish-white ring about 2 mm in width located close to but separated from the limbus . [MASK] generally occurs bilaterally, and is related to lipid deposition in the cornea. [MASK] can occur in elderly persons as a part of the aging process but may be associated with hypercholesterolemia in people under the age of 50 years.
A type of infection that is regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection because of unusual severity or intensity of the infection.
Scalp hair whose growth is slower than normal.
Underdevelopment of the sweat glands.
Increased width of the ischium, which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.
Acidosis because of respiratory retention of carbon dioxide.
A partial dislocation of one or more intervertebral joints in the cervical vertebral column.
A cleft of the lip with overlying mucous membrane.
Reduced diameter of the proximal phalanx of finger.
Reduced hydrolysis of the sulfuric ester linkage in the molecule of cerebroside sulfate, possibly leading to accumuation of cerebroside sulfate.
The gradual reduction in girth of the toe from proximal to distal.
An anomaly of a toe.
An anomaly of the patella characterized by two layers visible on lateral knee X-ray such that one layer is in front of the other in the sagittal orientation . This finding persists into adulthood.
An abnormality of calcium concentration in the urine.
Temper tantrums, which occur with more severe symptomatology compared to a temper tantrum that occurs as a part of normal developmental process.
Underdevelopment of the frontal bone.

[MASK] is characterized by air dissecting within the interstitium of the lung, typically in the peribronchovascular sheaths, interlobular septa, and visceral pleura. It is most commonly seen in neonates receiving mechanical ventilation. It is rarely recognized radiographically in adults and is infrequently seen on CT scans. It appears as perivascular lucent or low attenuating halos and small cysts.
Concentration of erythritol in the cerebrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal.
The concentration of ribose in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
Narrow, paramedian longitudinal depressions in the plantar skin of the forefoot.

No consensus exists on what a [MASK] is, but these episodes can be functionally defined as a new neurological deficit, occurring with or without the context of seizures, which last longer than 24 hours.
With the hand relaxed and the thumb in the plane of the palm, the axis of the thumb forms an angle of at least 90 degrees with the long axis of the hand.
An abnormal increase in the bone density of the long bones.
The relative concentration of deoxypyridinoline to that of pyridinoline cross-links in urine is above the upper limit of normal.

Decreased thickness of the glomerular basement membrane , measured from endothelial to visceral epithelial plasma membrane and mainly attributable to a decrease in thickness of the lamina densa, generally to an overall thickness more than 2 standard deviations less than that of the normal mean GBM thickness for health age- and sex matched individuals. May be focal or diffuse, although the term thin GBMs generally implies thinning of over 50% of GBMs.
Enamel with a white or brown discoloration without hypoplasia.
An increased concentration of histidine in the urine.
A deviation from normal signal on magnetic resonance imaging of the brainstem.
Uneven rhythm of breathing.
A rupture of the cornea through which a portion of the iris protrudes.

[MASK] is an abnormally flat shape of the cornea such that the normal protrusion of the cornea from the sclera is missing. The reduced corneal curvature can lead to hyperopia, and a hazy corneal limbus and arcus lipoides may develop at an early age.
A [MASK] is a congenital saccular dilatation of the distal segment of the ureter.
The amount of guanosine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
Increased concentration of guanosine in the blood circulation.
An increased concentration of orotic acid in the urine.
There is normally one ossification center in the head of the femur. This term applies if there are multiple such centers.
Persistent pain, usually defined as pain that has lasted longer than 3 to 6 months.

Presence in the urine of succinylacetone, which is one of the toic block metabolites formed in tyrosinaemia type 1 because of a defect in the final enzyme of the pathway of the degradation of tyrosine, namely fumarylacetoacetase .
A difference in length or diameter between the left and right leg.
Absence of one half of the vertebral body in the thoracic spine.

The fetal spleen is lobulated, and these lobules normally disappear before the birth. Lobulation of the spleen may persist into adult life and be typically seen along the medial part of the spleen. A persisting lobule results in a variation in shape of the spleen.

Significantly decreased level or failed detection of surfactant protein C in broncho-alveolar lavage fluid. Comment: Pulmonary surfactant is a highly surface-active mixture of proteins and lipids that is synthesized and secreted onto the alveoli by type II epithelial cells. The protein part of surfactant constitutes of four types of surfactant proteins , SP-A, SP-B, SP-C and SP-D. SP-A and SP-D are hydrophilic proteins that regulate surfactant metabolism and have immunologic functions, whereas SP-B and SP-C are hydrophobic molecules, which play a direct role in the organization of the surfactant structure in the interphase and in the stabilization of the lipid layers during the respiratory cycle. Lack of SP-C may result of surfactant metabolism dysfunction and is also observed in patients with other diffuse parenchymal lung diseases, pathogenetically related to the alveolar surfactant region.

A nodular pattern is characterized on pulmonary high-resolution computed tomography by the presence of numerous rounded opacities that range from 2 mm to 1 cm in diameter, with micronodules defined as smaller than 3 mm in diameter.

The so-called [MASK] appears as thickened interlobular septa and intralobular lines superimposed on a background of ground-glass opacity, resembling irregularly shaped paving stones. The [MASK] is often sharply demarcated from more normal lung and may have a geographic outline. It was originally reported in patients with alveolar proteinosis and is also encountered in other diffuse lung diseases that affect both the interstitial and airspace compartments, such as lipoid pneumonia.
Overproduction of adrenocorticotropic hormone , which generally leads secondarily to overproduction of cortisol by the adrenal cortex.
Activity of glucose-6-phosphate translocase in liver below the lower limit of normal.
Concentration or activity of fructose 1,6-bisphosphate aldolase in liver tissue below the lower limit of normal.
Chorioretinal atrophy along the retinal veins.
Upturned concavity of toenails.

A type of retinal detachment arising from damage to the outer blood-retinal barrier that allows fluid to access the subretinal space and separate the neurosensory retina from the retinal pigment epithelium.
Abnormal location of the ear.
Skin tastes marked salty without an obvious explanation such as heat or exercise. This finding can be observed in infants with cystic fibrosis.
The presence of a supernumerary, i.e. third, crus of the helix in the helix, arising at or above the normal bifurcation of the antihelix.
Any deviation from the normal motor coordination of the eyes that allows for bilateral fixation on a single object.
Multifocal slowing of cerebral electrical activity recorded along the scalp by electroencephalography .
Decreased width of the upper lip.
Absence or underdevelopment of the distal phalanges.
A type of crying in an abnormally high-pitched voice.
Delayed maturation and calcification of the rami of the pubic bone.
A lesion of the skin that is located in a specific region rather than being generalized.
Shortening of the middle parts of the leg in relation to the upper and terminal segments.
Bending or curvature of a third toe in the tibial direction .
An electric signal of depolarization observed between the end of the QRS complex and the beginning of the T wave.
An inflammation of the kidney involving the parenchyma of kidney, the renal pelvis and the kidney calices.
The presence of xanthine-containing calculi in the kidneys.
An increase in size of the anatomic space between the arachnoid membrane and pia mater in the region surrounding the cerebrum.

Abnormality of REM Sleep are phases of REM sleep are characterized by desynchronized EEG patterns, increases in heart rate and blood pressure, sympathetic activation, and a profound loss of muscle tone except for the eye and middle-ear muscles. There are also phases of rapid eye movements.
Conduction block in the posterior division of the left bundle branch of the bundle of His.
The presence of inclusion bodies within the cytoplasm of muscle cells. Inclusion bodies are aggregates or stainable material, usually misfolded proteins.
A structural abnormality of the peripheral nervous system, which is composed of the nerves that lead to or branch off from the central nervous system. This includes the cranial nerves .
A congenital form of torticollis resulting from shortening of the sternocleidomastoid muscle and leading to a limited range of motion in both rotation and lateral bending.
Congenital atresia of the pylorus.
Telangiectasia of the oral mucosa.
Abnormally small-sized handwriting is formally defined as an impairment of fine motor skills, which mainly manifests as a progressive or stable reduction in amplitude during a writing task.
Abnormally reduced concentration of ferritin, a ubiquitous intracellular protein that stores iron, in the blood.
Developmental delay of ossification of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
Supraventricular tachycardia in which an accessory pathway connecting the atria and ventricles, apart from the AV node, participates as a necessary part of a reentrant mechanism.
A clinically observable or self-reported abnormal behavior, experience, or physiological event that occurs in association with sleep, specific sleep stages, or sleep-wake transitions.
Fusion of the terminal/distal and middle phalanges of the 5th finger.
Sudden-onset episode of abnormal, involuntary eye movements.
An anomaly in the amount of force per unit area exerted by the intraocular fluid within the eye.
Increased depth of the anterior chamber, i.e., the anteroposterior distance between the cornea and the iris is increased.
Absence of transferrin, a protein that transports iron, in the blood.
Reduction in diameter of the ulna.
A wartlike papule.
A congenital diaphragm defect involving the central tendinous portion of the diaphragm, whereby the entire rim of diaphragmatic musculature is present.
Reduction in density of metaphyseal bony tissue.
Interruption of the procecss of diffferentiation of hematopoietic cells in the bone marrow, manifested by an increased proportion of immature cells in the bone marrow.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort and perceived to originate in the throat.
Increased size of platelet dense granules.
Activity of beta-ureidopropionase in the liver below the lower limit of normal.
The amount of N-carbamyl-beta-aminoisobutyric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
An abnormal gyral pattern characterized by abnormalities of sulcal depth or orientation.
An abnormal widening of the common carotid artery.
Abnormally increased caliber of the left subclavian artery.

Multiple verrucous lesions on the skin of the sole of the foot. These lesions are raised, have a thickened and rough surface, and may display prominent black dots . Palmar warts are caused by caused by human papillomavirus .

An abnormal result of a physical examination of the the hand that tests for palsy of the ulnar nerve. This nerve innervates the adductor pollicis and interossei muscles and thereby enables adduction of the thumb and extension of the interphalangeal joint. An abnormal result consists in reduced functionality and muscular weakness in the pinch grip between the thumb and index finger of the affected hand as the patient attempts to pinch a piece of paper that the examiner tries to pull away. The flexor pollicis longus muscle tries to compensate for the weakness by flexing the tip of the thumb at the interphalangeal joint.
A count of antral follicles that is lower than normal for age.

A [MASK] is a deeply ingrained pattern of behavior of a specified kind that deviates markedly from the norms of generally accepted behavior. It is typically apparent by the time of adolescence and causes long-term difficulties in personal relationships or functioning in society.
The presence of spots or rounded patches of abnormally increased density of metaphyseal bone.
Concentration of hepcidin in the blood circulation above the upper limit of normal.
Ingrowth of new blood vessels into the cornea.

[MASK] is characterized by widespread non inflammatory thorn-like follicular projections. Dyskeratotic papules are most pronounced over the extensor extremities and scalp and are symmetrically distributed.
An abnormal connection between a carotid artery and the cavernous sinus.
The presence of both ovarian and testicular tissues either in the same or in opposite gonads. Affected persons have ambiguous genitalia and may have 46,XX or 46,XY karyotypes or 46,XX/XY mosaicism.
A posterolateral defect in the diaphragm, commonly referred to as a [MASK], which is often accompanied by herniation of the stomach, intestines, liver, and/or spleen into the chest cavity.
Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface of the posterior cerebral artery.
Narrowing of the carotid arteries.
Increased muscle weakness upon exposure to cold temperatures.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood circulation.
Osteoporosis affecting predominantly the vertebrae.

An abnormality of pancreatic beta cells characterized by a proliferation of abnormal beta cells throughout the entire pancreas, with enlarged islet size and number , increased periductular islets, enlarged beta-cell nuclei and abundant clear cytoplasm. Occasionally beta cells with pleomorphic nuclei, ductuloinsular complexes, and neoformation of islets from ducts are observed.
Deficiency of secretory IgA and is the primary antibody response at the mucosal level, where it forms immune complexes with pathogens and allergens.
Increased concentration of potassium in the blood circulation specifically measured during a disease flareup, attack, or exacerbation.
An increase in the vertical distance between adjacent vertebral bodies, observed as an increase in the intervertebral disk space.

Mild pyelectasis is defined as a hypoechoic spherical or elliptical space within the renal pelvis that measures at least 5mm and not more than 10 mm. The measurement is taken on a transverse section through the fetal renal pelvis using the maximum anterior-to-posterior measurement.
Reduced plasmalogen concentration in the blood circulation.
A hemangioblastoma of the spinal cord.
A cystadenoma, an epithelial tumor, that originates within the head of the epididymis.
A [MASK]

[MASK] is a rare fatty tissue nevus that is a marker for encephalocraniocutaneous lipomatosis, a neurocutaneous syndrome with ocular and central nervous system anomalies. Clinically, [MASK] is often described as a congenital alopecia and appears as an irregularly shaped, circumscribed area of alopecia on the scalp. Histopathology demonstrates a near-complete absence of mature hair follicles with preservation of arrector pili muscles and mature adipocytes within the dermis.

Mild reduction of the ability to see. On the 6m visual acuity scale, mild reduction is defined as less than 6/12 but at least 6/18. On the 20ft visual acuity scale, mild reduction is defined as less than 20/40 but at least 20/70. On the decimal visual acuity scale, mild reduction is defined as less than 0.5 but at least 0.3.
A form of lactic acidemia with congenital onset.

A groove or crease on the shins . Pretibial creases may be obvious at birth and may range from 3 cm to over 15 cm in length and lengthen as the limb grows. They appear as an elongated dimple because of the attachment of skin to underlying tissue . The dimple or crease grows in proportion to the growth of the leg.
An abnormally increased activity of the renin-angiotensin system, causing hypertension by a combination of volume excess and vasoconstrictor mechanisms.
A type of pallor that is secondary to the presence of anemia.
A lacy pattern or iris pigmentation that resembles the spokes of a bicycle wheel.
Decreased length of the uvula.
Abnormally increased levels of lysine in cerebrospinal fluid.
An abnormal predominance of type II muscle fibers .
Increased concentration of neopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid .
Dysfunction of the urinary bladder.
Radiolucency around the apex .
Underdevelopment of the frontal part of the internal capsule.
A type of genetic anticipation observed predominantly upon transmission from affected males.
An abnormality of the shape of the lumbar vertebra L2 such that it is wedge-shaped .
An abnormal build up of iron in brain tissue.
A type of megaloblastic anemia that improves upon the administration of thiamine.
An abnormality of the metabolism of mucopolysaccharide.
An increased number of turns of the blood vessels of the nailfold with a charactereistic winded or twisted appearance of the blood vessels.
Enlargement of lymph nodes surrounding the trachea.
A type of ventricular tachycardia that is characterized by uniform QRS complexes within each lead .
An abnormality of the placenta in which there are numerous cystic spaces within the placenta as well as placental enlargement.
A discontinuity of the skin exhibiting incomplete loss of the epidermis, a lesion that is moist, circumscribed, and usually depressed.
The presence of an increased mass of red blood cells in the circulation.

An increased degree of femoral version, which is defined as the angular difference between axis of femoral neck and transcondylar axis of the knee. Thus, femoral anteversion is an inward twisting of the femur that causes the knees and feet to turn inward.
Multiple cysts along the pupillary margin that appear as spherical or tear-drop-shaped pigmented lesions or wrinkled masses emerging from the pupillary border of the iris.
Increased width of the ulna.
[MASK], which is the fluid contained in the amniotic sac surrounding the developing fetus.
A foot deformity resulting due to an abnormality affecting the muscle and soft tissue. In contrast if the bones of the foot are affected the term structural foot deformity applies.
Narrowing of the distance between lumbar vertebral pedicles that gets progressively more severe towards to caudal end of the vertebral column.
[MASK] results from progressive calcium deposition along and beneath the mitral valve annulus.
The union of two separately developing tooth germs typically leading to one less tooth than normal in the affected dental arch.
An abnormality of the functioning of any aspect of the alternative complement pathway.
Abnormal increased size of the elbow joint.
All of the metacarpal bones of the hand have a pointed proximal appearance.
Activity of the enzyme alpha-L-fucosidase below the lower limit of normal.

The presence of an abnormally increased concentration of neutral amino acids in the urine. The neutral amino acids are tryptophan, alanine, asparagine, glutamine, histidine, isoleucine, leucine, phenylalanine, serine, threonine, tyrosine and valine.
Atrophy of the frontal cortex.
Activity of L-arginine:glycine amidinotransferase in the tissues below the lower limit of normal. GATM activity can be measured in multiple tissues including leukocytes and cultured fibroblasts.
Displacement of the 5th finger from its normal position.
Abnormally increased levels of alanine in cerebrospinal fluid.
Tremor of the trunk in an anterior-posterior plane at 3-4 Hz.
A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging of the pons.
Concentration of argininosuccinic acid in the cerebrospinal fluid above the upper limit of normal.
Atrophy of the temporal cortex.
The presence of distinct colors in the central zone of the iris than in the mid-peripheral zone.
Abnormal increased size of the viscera of the abdomen.
Decreased level of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase . ALDH and alcohol dehydrogenase are the primary enzymes involved in alcohol metabolism.
Congenital absence of one or more limbs.
An increased concentration of cystine within cells. This finding can be demonstrated on leukocytes, but is not specific to blood cells.
The presence of intracellular inclusion bodies in neurons that stain with eosin, a red or pink dye.
An impairment of a fructose metabolic process.
Multiple beaded papules along the eyelid margins and inner canthus.
Longstanding abnormal acid accumulation or depletion of base.

Formation of lumps of tonofilaments, which are bundles of keratin filaments. In some but not all epithelia, keratin filaments are conspicuously bundled as tonofilaments. Inside the cell they braid the nucleus, span through the cytoplasm and are attached to the cytoplasmic plaques of the typical epithelial cell-cell junctions, the desmosomes.
An abnormal limitation of the mobility of the wrist.
Underdevelopment of the lower eyelid.
Bending or curvature of the distal phalanx of little finger in the radial direction .
A deviation from the normal concentration of beta-C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen in the blood circulation, a marker of the rate of bone turnover.

An excessive division of the lobes of the nucleus of eosinophils. Eosinophils with more than two nuclear lobes are commonly regarded as hypersegmented, because seventy to ninety percent of peripheral blood eosinophils have two nuclear lobes.
Two-sided or bilateral weakness of the muscles of facial expression and eye closure.

Disseminated multifocal hemangiomatous or lymphangiomatous lesions of the skeleton. The lesions are lytic, well-defined, round or oval lesions within the medullary cavity, and they have an intact cortex, and manifest variable peripheral sclerosis and may exhibit endosteal scalloping.

Activity of the gycogen debrancher enzyme in muscle tissue is below the lower limit of normal. GDE is a large monomeric protein with two catalytic activities: amylo-1,6-glucosidase and 4-alpha-glucanotransferase .

Diffusely widened perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia, affecting especially the corpus striatum. [MASK] is usually symmetrical, with the perivascular spaces showing CSF signal and without diffusion restriction. The word cribriform means sievelike, with multiple perforations.
Best corrected visual acuity worse than 1.90 logMAR .
Reduced number of primary teeth.
Localized thickening and tightness of the skin of the fingers or toes.
Any structural anomaly of the mitochondria.
Interphalangeal joint stiffness is a perceived sensation of tightness in the interphalangeal joints when attempting to move them after a period of inactivity.
Impaired conduction of cardiac impulse occurring anywhere along the conduction pathway.
Dilatation of the bladder postnatally.

[MASK] is a rare anomaly characterized by placentomegaly, dilatation of chorionic vessels and hydropic stem villi with cistern-like formation. It is often clinically mistaken for a partial hydatidiform mole but there is no trophoblastic proliferation. P57 immunohistochemical expression is discordant, showing a normal positive expression in the cytotrophoblastic cells, and loss of expression in the stromal cells.
Hyperplasia of the pancreas.
Longitudinal, linear prominences in the fingernail plate.

An increased level of 17-hydroxyprogesterone in the blood. 17-hydroxyprogesterone is an intermediate steroid in the adrenal biosynthetic pathway from cholesterol to cortisol and is the substrate for steroid 21-hydroxylase.
Hypospadias with location of the urethral meatus in the scrotum.
An abnormal conformation of the femur that becomes gradually enlarged towards the distal end. This feature affects the distal femoral metaphysis and epiphysis.
Uneven increase in bone density of one or more of the phalanges of the hand.
The concentration of serum amyloid A in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.
The activity of 6-pyruvoyltetrahydropterin synthase in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
An increase in the level of galactitol in the plasma.
A tooth that has not erupted because of local impediments .
Inability to see well at night or in poor light with onset in adulthood.
A tumor of the uterine cervix.
Tearing of the aortic wall generally associated with profuse internal bleeding.
Calcified deposits in soft tissue structures outside a joint.
An accumulation of calcium and phosphate in arteries with mineral deposits in the intimal or medial layer of the vessel wall of the femoral artery.

An [MASK] , i.e., of the electrical signals of sensation going from the body to the brain in response to a defined stimulus. Recording electrodes are placed over the scalp, spine, and peripheral nerves proximal to the stimulation site. Clinical studies generally use electrical stimulation of peripheral nerves to elicit potentials. SSEP testing determines whether peripheral sensory nerves are able to transmit sensory information like pain, temperature, and touch to the brain. Abnormal SSEPs can result from dysfunction at the level of the peripheral nerve, plexus, spinal root, spinal cord, brain stem, thalamocortical projections, or primary somatosensory cortex.
A benign tumor originating from the outer root sheath of the hair follicle.
Abnormally persistent clusters of embryonal cells, representing microscopic malformations of the developing kidney.
A type of diabetic metabolic abnormality with an accumulation of ketone bodies.
An early onset of puberty, in this case early does not refer to precocious.
Mirror image atrial arrangement, with morphologic right atrium on the left hand side and morphologic left atrium on the right hand side.
Lack of ossification of the sacrum.
Reduction in the amount of blood flow to the iris.
Blockage of the retinal vein.
Deposition of fibrillar material that can be found on all anterior segment structures bathed by aqueous humor.
A loss of the ability to move the vocal fold on one side.
Calcification in the laryngeal tissues.
An decrease in the level of glutamine in the brain identified by magnetic resonance spectroscopy .
A type of arrhythmia that originates above the ventricles, whereby the electrical impulse propagates down the normal His Purkinje system similar to normal sinus rhythm.
Distal epiphyses of the hand are hard and dense like ivory. Such an epiphysis has a uniformly dense appearance on radiographs.
[MASK] is an abnormal location of the heart in which the heart is in a midline position and the longitudinal axis of the heart lies in the mid-sagittal plane.
Pheochromocytoma originating from the adrenal medulla.
A type of [MASK].
Repeated episodes of headache with rapid onset, reaching a peak within minutes and of short duration with pain that is throbbing, pulsating, or bursting in quality.
Hypoplasia of the distal phalanx of the third finger.

Chronic active Epstein-Barr virus infection is an uncommon outcome of EBV infection and may present as a waxing and waning or fulminant syndrome. Unlike acute infectious mononucleosis, wherein EBV establishes lifelong infection and survives by maintaining a delicate balance with the host as a latent infection, in chronic active EBV infection the host-virus balance is disturbed.

An [MASK] is a thin sheet of fibrous tissue that can develop on the surface of the macular area of the retina and cause a disturbance in vision. An [MASK] area can develop on the thin macular area of the retin. An [MASK] is also sometimes called a [MASK], [MASK], surface wrinkling retinopathy or cellophane maculopathy.
Activity or concentration of in the level of porphobilinogen deaminase in erythrocytes below the lower limit of normal.
An abnormal narrowing of the spinal canal related to a reduction in the interpedicular distance .
Presence of multiple hyperplastic polyps in the colon. Hyperplastic polyps are generally about 5 mm in size and show hyperplastic mucosal proliferation.
Characteristic appearance of the chest and abdomen in the sagittal view on prenatal ultrasound when the chest is small and the abdomen protruding.

Increase in diameter of a segment of the renal artery that can be defined as a focal, isolated dilatation of all three layers of the arterial wall over 1.5 times the diameter of the disease-free proximal adjacent arterial segment.
Any abnormality of the primary tooth.
The concentration of dihydrouracil in the cerebrospinal fluid is above the upper limit of normal.
Concentration of the nucleobase thymine in the blood circulation above the normal range.
Concentration of uracil in the blood circulation is above the normal range.

[MASK] is a descriptive term that should be avoided if more precise information is available. However, the HPO keeps retains this term because it is commonly used in the medical literature. In humans, the process of thyroid morphogenesis occurs from the 3rd to 16th week of gestation. Alterations occurring during this period may result in a thyroid gland that is absent , hypoplastic , or located in an unusual position . All these entities are grouped under the term [MASK].
This term refers to the [MASK] that were previously present.
A complete lack of the ability to track objects with the ocular smooth pursuit system, a class of rather slow eye movements that minimizes retinal target motion.
Spasticity in the muscles of the tongue.

Hepatic failure refers to the inability of the liver to perform its normal synthetic and metabolic functions, which can result in coagulopathy and alteration in the mental status of a previously healthy individual. Hepatic failure is defined as fulminant if there is onset of encephalopathy within 4 weeks of the onset of symptoms in a patient with a previously healthy liver.
Underdevelopment of the neurohypophysis.

[MASK] are yellow-orange-to-red-brown papules that are often surrounded by an erythematous halo. They appear in crops on the buttocks, extensor surfaces of the extremities, and flexural creases. Acutely, variable amounts of pruritus and pain occur.
An elevated concentration of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in the blood.
Atrophy of the muscles of the ankle.
Shoulder dislocation occurring repeated times.

An anomalous trapezoidal appearance of a vertebral body. A trapezoid is a four-sided shape that has two sides that are parallel and two sides that are not parallel. In this case, the two lateral sides of the vertebra are parallel, and the top and the bottom are slanted with respect to each other such that the vertebra is shorter in the front or back than on the other side.
Abnormally reduced diameter of the clavicles that is limited to the distal region.

A generalized motor seizure is a type of generalized-onset seizure with predominantly motor signs. The motor event could consist of an increase or decrease in muscle contraction to produce a movement.
One or more previous pregnancies resulted in stillbirth, defined as death of a fetus in the later stages of pregnancy .
Reduction in the anterosuperior prominence of the area between the bottom of the incisura and the inner margin of the antihelix.
[MASK] refers to congenital or acquired fixation of the incus, which is associated with conductive hearing resulting from impairment of the sound-conduction mechanism .

Hyperpigmented macules with a reticulate pattern involving the neck, axillae, groins, and other flexures like the inframammary folds in females. Histopathology shows orthokeratosis or hyperkeratosis, thinning of the suprapapillary epithelium, elongation of the rete ridges, hyperpigmentation of the basal layer, and follicular cysts. A perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate can be observed in the papillary dermis.
Persistence of the urachal canal resulting in a canal between the bladder and the umbilicus.
[MASK] can be measured as the absence of the caloric nystagmus response in electronystagmography.
Cardiac arrest that would have led to rapid and unexpected death had an intervention not taken place to prevent it.
The length of the incisura from the upper to lower border is greater than that observed in the average population.
Concentration or activity of Peptidase D below the lower limit of normal. The activity of this enzyme can be measured in erythrocytes, leukocytes, or fibroblasts.
Absence of the acoustic reflex, an involuntary contraction of the stapedius muscle that occurs in response to high-intensity sound stimuli.
The presence of a [MASK], thereby creating a vaginal duplication.
A non-midline cleft of the upper lip on one side only.

An intermittent esotropia with binocular single vision present at distance fixation but esotropia on accommodation for near fixation. Usually associated with hypermetropia but patients can be emmetropic and rarely myopic. Associated with a high accommodative convergence/accommodation ratio.
A softening and breaking down of skin resulting from prolonged exposure to moisture. Macerated skin becomes soft and wrinkly and takes on a whitish hue.
Alteration or impairment in the processing or interpretation of sensory information can lead to abnormal perceptions or experiences.
Abnormally high concentration of coproporphyrin 3 in feces
Inflammation of the cartilage of the external ear.
Unusual prominence of the median palatal raphe, which is the ridge formed by the fusion of the two plates of the skull that form the hard palate.
Increased size of the placenta.
An elevated level of insulin-like growth factor 1 in the blood circulation.
Bullae of the skin with an acral distribution .
Partial or complete wasting of dentate nucleus.
Abnormally elevated blood carbon dioxide level.
Increased vertical distance from the vermillion border of the lower lip to the inferior-most point of the chin.
[MASK] are extracellular deposits of amyloid in the gray matter of the brain.
A tumor formed from the endocrine cells of the mucosal lining of a variety of organs including the stomach and intestine. These cells are from neuroectodermal origin.
A neuroendocrine tumor originating in a hormone-producing cell of the pancreas.
An abnormal accumulation of protein in the glomerulus.
Accumulation of fibronectin in the glomerulus.
Abnormally increased levels of leucine in cerebrospinal fluid.
Any increased amount from normal of valine in the cerebrospinal fluid.
Presence of IgG antibodies in the dermoepidermal junction that are distributed in a linear pattern. This feature can be appreciated by immunofluorescence microscopy.
Absence of the radial spokes of the axoneme of the respiratory cilium.
An increased susceptibility to viral upper respiratory tract infections as manifested by a history of [MASK] .
A membrane-like structure that extends across the laryngeal lumen close to the level of the vocal cords.
Presence of N-acetylglucosamine-rich oligosaccharides in the urine.
An abnormally increased diphosphate concentration in the blood. Diphosphate, as ester with two phosphate groups, is also known as pyrophosphate.
Deposition of calcium salts in point-like foci within the anterior portion of one or more ribs.
A partial or complete breakage of the rib.
Ultra-low vision but with retained ability to identify a moving object .
A type of retinal exudate located in the subretinal space between the sensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.
