[MASK] is a rare congenital airway malformation in which distinct tracheal rings are replaced by a continuous cartilaginous segment. Vertically fused C- or O-shaped cartilaginous rings can extend from the subglottis to the carina or bronchus with little to no pars membranacea posteriorly. Comment:[MASK] has been associated with various craniosynostosis syndromes.
A soft tissue continuity in the anteroposterior axis between the toes 3 and 4.
Proliferation of hemopoietically active tissue or of tissue which has embryonic hemopoietic potential.
A decreased concentration of potassium in the urine.
Incisor teeth with irregular edges said to resemble a saw.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against muscle specific kinase .

Increased concentration of 11-deoxycortisol in the circulation. 11-deoxycorticosterone, which is also known as simply deoxycorticosterone and 21-hydroxyprogesterone, is a steroid hormore that is produces in the adrenals and is a precursor to aldosterone.
Activity of mannosyl-oligosaccharide glucosidase in tissues below the lower limit of normal. MOGS activity can be measured in multiple tissues including liver and cultured fibroblasts.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of a lipid in the blood circulation.
Activity of isovaleryl-CoA dehydrogenase below the lower limit of normal in cultured fibroblasts.
The concentration of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
The concentration of interleukin-6 in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

A type of retinal detachment associated with a retinal tear, that is, with a break in the retina that allows fluid to pass from the vitreous space into the subretinal space between the sensory retina and the retinal pigment epithelium.
An abnormality of the medullary cavity , which is the central cavity of bone shafts where red bone marrow and/or yellow bone marrow is stored.
An abnormality of the concentration of glucose in the blood.

An increased concentration of tropnin I in the blood, which is a cardiac regulatory protein that controls the calcium mediated interaction between actin and myosin. Raised cardiac troponin concentrations are now accepted as the standard biochemical marker for the diagnosis of myocardial infarction.
Absence of the anterior chamber of the eye owing to a developmental defect.
Concentration of alpha-fetoprotein in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
A developmental defect characterized by the absence of the first metatarsal bone.
Level of methionine in urine above the upper limit of normal.
Any abnormality of the size or morphology of the cornea.
A reduction in phenylalanine 4-monooxygenase level.

Any deviation from the normal amount of time to coagulation in the prothrombin time test, which is a measure of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation. The results of the prothrombin time test are often expressed in terms of the International normalized ratio , which is calculated as a ratio of the patient's prothrombin time to a control PT standardized for the potency of the thromboplastin reagent developed by the World Health Organization using the formula: INR is equal to Patient PT divided by Control PT.
A lower than normal concentration of citrate in the urine.
Episodes of fever for which no infectious cause can be identified.

Increased susceptibility to gastroenteritis, an infectious inflammationof the stomach and small intestines manifested by signs and symptoms such as diarheas and abdominal pain, as manifested by recurrent episodes of gastroenteritis.
Mineralized substance filling the entire dental pulp space.
A decreased level of glucose-6-phosphate isomerase.
An increased amount of 4-hydroxybutyric acid in the urine.
Elevated concentration of gamma-aminobutyric acid in the urine.
An aberrant thyroid gland or Ectopic thyroid located at the base of the tongue, just posterior to the foramen cecum as a result of a failure of the thyroid to descend.
Inflammation of the uveal tract in which inflammation affects the anterior chamber, vitreous, retina or choroid.
A type of blistering that affects the skin of the tibial region.
Involuntary contraction or twitching of the muscles.
Dilated blood vessels on the skin.
Concentration of 3-hydroxyisovaleric acid in the urine above the normal range.
Osteomyelitis caused by infection with the bacteria, salmonella.
A developmental defect characterized by fusion of the left and right halves of the thalamus.

Conduct and/or behavior, both verbal and non-verbal, including but not limited to verbal and/or physical aggression, attacks, threats, harassment, intimidation, and other disruptive behaviors in any form or through any medium, that cause or have the potential to cause a reasonable person to fear physical harm from any individual or group towards any person or property. This is commonly defined as a violent act characterized by the use of physical force, anger, or sudden intense activity.
Increased space between the primary teeth. Note this phenotype should be distinguished from increased space due purely to microdontia.
A lack of ossification of the vertebral bodies.
An anomaly of the femoral metaphysis.
A lasting decrease of immunoglobulin G1 in the blood.
Abnormally low amount of sulfur in hair.
Any structural anomaly of the hippocampus,

An increase in the distance between vertebral pedicles, which are the two short, thick processes, which project backward, one on either side, from the upper part of the vertebral body, at the junction of its posterior and lateral surfaces.
The presence of a fistula affecting the rectum.
Anomaly of the visual evoked potentials elicited by a flash stimulus, generally a flash of light subtending an angle of at least 20 degrees of the visual field and presented in a dimly lit room.
Any defect in the valve connecting the heart and the pulmonary artery.
Underdevelopment of the alveolar process .
An abnormal accumulation of fluid beneath the skin, or in one or more cavities of the body because of decreased osmotic pressure of plasma .
The amount of 2,8-dihydroxyadenine in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.
An increased concentration of insulin in the blood in the fasting state, i.e., not as the response to food intake.
An acute form of hepatic steatosis.
An increased density in the cranial sutures following obliteration.
Abnormal increase of the activated HLA-DR+ CD4+ T cell subpopulation, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.
A chronic form of lymphadenopathy that is not related to infection.
A type of chronic kidney disease with severely reduced glomerular filtration rate .

The [MASK] is one of the most characteristic skin findings. It commonly occurs on the soles of the feet, and frequently causes problems because of pain, pruritus, infection, bleeding,exudation, odor, and walking impairment.

A type of pituitary adenoma originating in prolactin secreting cells. This kind of adenoma is characterized by overproduction of prolactin, and may cause loss of menstrual periods and breast milk production in women.
Activity or concentration of inosine triphosphate pyrophosphohydrolase in red blood cells below the lower limit of normal.
An abnormal reduction in the number of mitochondria in hepatocytes.

The sacroiliac joint in the bony pelvis connects the sacrum and the ilium of the pelvis, which are joined by strong ligaments. The notch is located directly superior to the joint. This term refers to a increase in the lateral dimension of the notch.
The presence of multiple hemangiomas in the choroid. These are generally reddish or orange or can have increased pigmentation maiking them difficult to distinguish from choroidal melanomas.
The severe form of a neural tube defect where the open neural tube appears as a flattened, plate-like mass of nervous tissue with no overlying membrane.
Presence of a lipoma in the region of the sacrum.

A [MASK] is an abnormality present at birth over the dorsal midline where an abnormal epithelialized connection from the skin tracks inwards towards the spine, most commonly seen in the lumbosacral region.
Activity of the enzyme alpha-1,4-glucosidase activity in muscle tissue is below the lower limit of normal.
Focal epileptiform EEG discharges recorded in the occipital region.
Focal epileptiform EEG discharges recorded in the parietal region.
Reduced activity of the enzyme acid sphingomyelinase activity in the blood circulation.
Reduced ability to absorb folate in the diet. This finding can be measured by a folic acid loading test in which blood concentration of folate is measured after oral administration of folic acid.

Multiple multiple, small, well-defined radiodense foci of cortical-like bone in the medullary space parallel to the trabeculae located in the femur. The loci correspond to condensations of the lamellar trabeculae on histology.
[MASK] are hamartomas in which one or several components of the dermis is altered.
Abnormally increased density of craniofacial bone tissue.
Intermittent episodes of increased resistance to the passage of air in the upper airway.
A coloboma of the ciliary body.
Abnormal increase of TCR gamma/delta positive T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group.
A structural abnormality of the sperm tail.
Increased density of the compact bone of long bone.

The presence of abnormally large granules in neutrophils. This finding can be appreciated on a peripheral blood smear. The finding is characteristic of Chediak Higashi syndrome. The giant granules are derived from azurophil granules, whereas peroxidase-negative granules are not involved in their formation.
Increased susceptibility to systemic pyogenic infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of systemic pyogenic infections.
The presence of a neoplasm of the testis.

A type of anomalous trichromacy associated with defective long-wavelength-sensitive cones, causing the sensitivity spectrum to be shifted toward medium wavelengths. This leads to difficulties especially in distinguishing red and green.
The presence of erythrocytes that are sphere-shaped and reduced in size.

Applied to a sign, symptom, or other manifestation that occurs multiple times at usually irregular intervals. The occurrences are separated by an interval in which the sign, symptom, or manifestation is not present.

An abnormal bone marrow finding characterized by many poorly circumscribed and occasionally confluent lymphoid nodules. The nodules contain small and uniform lymphocytes with rounded nuclei, clumped chromatin, and without prominent nucleoli.
Morphologically similar to a papule, but greater than either 10mm in both width and depth, and most frequently centered in the dermis or subcutaneous fat.

Resistance of the extensor muscles of the neck to being bent forwards as a result of muscle spasm of the extensor muscles of the neck. [MASK] is not a fixed rigidity. [MASK] has been used as a bedside test for [MASK], although its sensitivity for this purpose has been debated.

Abnormally increased levels of methemoglobin in the blood. In this form of hemoglobin, there is an oxidized ferric iron rather than the reduced ferrous form that is normally found in hemoglobin. Methemoglobin has a reduced affinity for oxygen, resulting in a reduced ability to release oxygen to tissues.
A reduced concentration of dehydroepiandrosterone-sulfate in the blood.
Inability to recognize faces of familiar persons.
A complete duplication of the ureter, where the duplicated ureters have separate insertions into the bladder.

An abnormally increased level of circulating alpha-globulin. Alpha globulins are a group of serum proteins defined by their mobility on serum electrophoresis. The alpha1-protein fraction is comprised of alpha1-antitrypsin, thyroid-binding globulin, and transcortin. Ceruloplasmin, alpha2-macroglobulin, and haptoglobin contribute to the alpha2-protein band. The alpha2 component is increased as an acute-phase reactant.
The concentration of calprotectin in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal.

A double outlet right ventricle with a ventricular spetal defect of the heart), that is considered to be closely related to the pulmonary origin. There is not associated pulmonary stenosis, the abnormal narrowing or constriction of the pulmonary artery, in the main pulmonary artery and/or in the left or right pulmonary artery branches.
Abnormality of an amino acid metabolic process.
Abnormality of the homeostasis of a monoatomic ion.
Any [MASK], i.e., of roof of the mouth.

An anomaly of epiphysis, which is the expanded articular end of a long bone that developes from a secondary ossification center, and which during the period of growth is either entirely cartilaginous or is separated from the shaft by a cartilaginous disk.

An elevated amount of uptake on the radioactive iodine uptake test, which utilizes a radioisotope of iodine to measure how much iodine the thyroid gland absorbs from the blood. The radioactive marker is measured 4-6 hours and in some cases also 24 hours after administration of the radioactive marker.
A medical history of a fetus or child born to a mother with an autoimmune disease.

A [MASK] is a benign vascular neoplasm that arises almost exclusively in the central nervous system. Hemangioblastomas consist of a tightly packed cluster of small blood vessels forming a mass of up to 1 or 2 cm in diameter.
Swelling from fluid accumulation in the cerebellum.
The presence of multiple rectal hyperplastic/adenomatous polyps.
An abnormality of compact bone , which forms the dense surface of bones.
Naevus flammeus localized in the skin of the eyelid.
A tumor of the head and neck region with origin in the lip, oral cavity, nasal cavity, paranasal sinuses, pharynx, or larynx.

Atrophy of one side of the brain, characterized by findings including thinning of the cerebral cortex, reduced volume of the cerebral white matter with abnormal myelination, and enlargement of the ispilateral fourth ventricle.
Obstruction of the flow of urine through the urethra.
A tumor of the thymus.
An abnormality of the structure of the veins that return deoxygenated blood from the body into the heart, i.e., the superior vena cava and the inferior vena cava.
An anomalous sound produced by the breathing process.
Absence or underdevelopment of the abdominal musculature.
Arthrosis, i.e., of degenerative joint disease, affecting the cervical vertebral column.
The presence of autoantibodies in the blood circulation that react against ribosome Po.
Acral or periorificial lesions that evolve in recurrent crops, with an annular and migratory distribution.
A papule that exhibits increased pigmentation compared to the surrounding skin.
An abnormally elevated concentration of total tryptase in the blood circulation.
A structural anomaly of the nervous system.
Any anomaly in the function of thrombocytes.

A condition in which the pituitary gland is partially resistant to thyroid hormone, so that it continues to secrete thyroid-stimulating hormone until the blood level of thyroid hormone rises higher than normal.

Post-exertional symptom exacerbation , also referred to as post-exertional malaise , is defined as the worsening of symptoms that can follow minimal cognitive, physical, emotional, or social activity, or activity that could previously be tolerated. Symptoms typically worsen 12 to 72 hours after activity and can last for days or even weeks, sometimes leading to a relapse.
Any anomaly of cell structure.
A multidimensional but common male sexual dysfunction that involves an alteration in any of the components of the erectile response, including organic, relational and psychological.
Neurodegeneration involving the globus pallidus,a part of the basal ganglia that is involved in the regulation of voluntary movement.
An anomaly in the amount or timing of melatonin secretion by the pineal gland. Note that melatonin is also synthesized by multiple tissues outside of the pineal gland.
Elastic fibers in the dermis exhibit an increased number of breaks associated with disorganization of the structure of the elastic fibers.
Increased pigmentation, either focal or generalized, of the mucosa of the mouth.
A rare pediatric carcinoma of the pancreas.
Hemorrhage between the skull and periosteum of a newborn resulting from rupture of blood vessels that cross the periosteum.
Golden brown or gray deposits with a clockwise, whorl-like distribution in the inferior interpalpebal portion of the cornea.
A sudden, irresistible need to have a bowel movement.
An anomaly of the calf bone , one of the two bones of the calf.
An unpleasant sensation characterized by physical discomfort localized to a tendon.
A contained rupture of an artery with a disruption in all 3 layers of the arterial wall.

A deviation from the normal concentration in blood of an apolipoprotein, i.e., of a protein that binds lipids to form lipoprotein and is thereby responsible for the transport of lipids in the blood and lymph circulation.

An [MASK], which is a region and not an anatomical term. It extends, superiorly, from the inferior orbital margin to, inferiorly, the level of nasal base. It is formed by the maxilla and zygoma and cheeks and malar region. Traditionally, the nose and premaxilla are not included in the midface.
A problem occurring during any phase of the male sexual response cycle that prevents the individual from experiencing satisfaction from the sexual activity
A type of infection of the skin that can be regarded as a sign of a pathological susceptibility to infection.
Blockage of the retinal artery, generally associated with interruption of blood flow and oxygen delivery to the retina.
Sensorineural hearing impairment with childhood onset.
A severe form of hearing impairment.
An abnormaltiy of the rectum, the final segment of the large intestine that stores solid waste until it passes through the anus.
History of repeated intermittent involuntary muscle contractions that were painful.
A focal type of palmoplantar keratoderma in which only certain areas of the palms and soles are affected.
Habitual biting of one's own fingernails.
Complete lack of abdominal sounds as assayed by examination of the abdomen with a stethoscope.
An anomaly of the muscular contractions that propel food though the gastrointestinal tract.
Any structural anomaly of the pulmonary valve leaflets.
The concentration of vitamin B1 in the blood circulation is below the lower limit of normal.
Abnormal appearance of material expectorated from the respiratory system and that is composed of mucus but may contain other substances such as pus, blood, microorganisms, and fibrin.
Reduced desire for sexual activity on the part of a male.
An abnormality of the lobule of pinna.
The amount of a nitrogen compound in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is outside of normal limits.
An abnormal shape or form of the proximal phalanx of the big toe.
Underdevelopment of the optic nerve and absence of the septum pellucidum.
The concentration of an interleukin is outside the limits of normal.
An increased concentration of interleukin-18 in the blood circulation.

The concentration of soluble FASL in the blood circulation is above the upper limit of normal. The first apoptosis signal receptor pathway regulates apoptosis and is critical for proper development and functioning of the immune system. FAS ligand can bind to FAS receptors.
An abnormality of the cardiac ventricular function.
Inflammation of the pharynx.
Difference in length or size between the right and left arm.
Focal EEG discharges that secondarily spread to both hemispheres and can then be recorded over the entire scalp.
An [MASK], the bony framework of the head which is comprised of the neurocranium and the viscerocranium that comprises fourteen facial bones with the mandible as its largest bone.
A palpable, solid lesion greater than 5mm in diameter that is located in the mucosa of the mouth.
The presence of an altered number of of teeth.
Repeated episodes of obstruction of blood flow due to an embolus, i.e., blood clot that has traveled from its point of origin within the blood stream.

An anomalous response to a medication related to individual variation in metabolic or immune response to drugs varying from potentially from potentially life-threatening adverse drug reactions to alteration of therapeutic efficacy.
Absence or underdevelopment of the iris.
Underdevelopment or absence of the uvula.
Terminal broadening of the toes .
Atrophy of the parietal cortex.
The presence of aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of all or part of the external ear.
Cleft between the helix and the lobe.

The vestibulo-ocular reflex is responsible for the stabilization of the retinal image during movement. The visual vestibular ocular reflex or visual enhanced VOR, maintains ocular stability during head motion by generating compensatory eye movement opposite to head movement, and is a major component of visual vestibular interaction. This feature is an impairment of this reflex, manifested as the combined impairment of the three compensatory eye movement reflexes, namely the vestibulo-ocular reflex , smooth pursuit and optokinetic reflex .
A functional abnormality affecting one or more of the cranial nerves, which emerge directly from the brain stem.
An abnormality of the melanosomes, i.e., of the cellular organelles in which melanin pigments are synthesized and stored within melanocytes .

Abnormally decreased length of time required for an in vitro clot to dissolve in the absence of the normal plasmin inhibitors. This test is a clinical assay used to measure fibrinolysis. The euglobulin fraction of plasma is precipitated and used to form clot by addition of thrombin; after clot forms the rate of clot breakdown can be monitored.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react to seven proteins that consist of a core of small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particles.
[MASK] of the skull.

The presence of multiple juvenile polyps in the stomach and intestine. The term juvenile polyps refer to a special histopathology and not the age of onset as the polyp might be diagnosed at all ages. The juvenile polyp has a spherical appearance and is microscopically characterized by overgrowth of an oedematous lamina propria with inflammatory cells and cystic glands. Juvenile polyps are a specific type of hamartomatous polyps.
The presence of an abnormal connection between the urethra and another organ or the skin.
An impairment of the electrical continuity between the atria and ventricles.
An abnormal concentration of potassium.
A form of hemolytic anemia with congenital onset.
Calcium deposits in the prostate gland.
A state of increased circulating antidiuretic hormone despite hyponatremia and hypo-osmolality with normal or increased plasma volume.
A sudden attack of dyspnea that occurs while the affected person is at rest.
[MASK] is characterized by bursts of laughter or giggling, usually without appropriate related emotion of happiness, and described as 'mirthless'.
Malfunction of a peripheral nerve resulting from mechanical compression of the nerve roots from internal or external causes and leading to a conduction block or axonal loss.
An abnormality of the function of the skeletal system.
One sided alveolar cleft of the maxilla.
Absence or underdevelopment of the mandible.
Having only one testis in the scrotum.
A abnormal increase in the inflammatory response to injury or infection.
An anomaly of the joint that connects the foot with the leg.
An abnormality of the thyroid gland owing to the presence of a fibrous cyst resulting from the persistence of the thyroglossal duct.
[MASK] can be a consequence of otologic disease , or can arise from pathologic processes and structures other than the ear .
A type of pituitary adenoma that produces growth hormone.
Slowed relaxation of muscles in the jaw.

[MASK] is a perceptual vocal quality that is gurgly or liquid sounding and is due to the voice being produced through moisture. It is commonly used as an indicator of penetration and/or aspiration in clinical swallowing assessments and bedside screening tests.

A reduction in the blood concentration of an androgen, that is, of a steroid hormone that controls development and maintenance of masculine characteristics. The androgens include testosterone and Dehydroepiandrosterone.
An anomaly of the outer labia.
An elevated concentration of progesterone in the blood.
Abnormally reduced blood carbon dioxide level.
Any anomaly of ovarian function.

Partial or complete wasting of muscularois propria tissue that was once present. The atrophy may involve a marked vacuolar degeneration of myocytes, loss of muscle fibers and some cases a highly characteristic honeycomb fibrosis.
Absence or underdevelopment of the clavicles .

Folds of membranous tissue attached to the wall of the abdomen and enclosing viscera. Examples include the mesentery for the small intestine; the transverse mesocolon, which attaches the transverse portion of the colon to the back wall of the abdomen; and the mesosigmoid, which enfolds the sigmoid portion of the colon. Cells of the same embryologic origin also surround the other organs of the body such as the lungs or the heart .
Any anomaly of the P wave of the EKG, which results from atrial depolarization. The P wave occurs when the sinoatrial node creates an action potential that depolarizes the atria.
Hyperresponsive to sound that is abnormal in intensity and/or frequency.
The presence of verrucous, cobblestone-like papules and nodules in a region of skin that is said to have an appearance like that of cobblestones.
Weakness of both lower extremities with sparing of the upper extremities. Paraplegia refers to a severe or complete loss of strength, whereas paraparesis refers to a relatively mild loss of strength.
A myxoma originating in the skin.
An anomaly of the mobility of ejaculated sperm.
An abnormality of the pulmonary situs, i.e., of the sidedness of the morphological right and left lungs, in which the morphology of both left and right lungs is the same.

Thickening of the peribronchovascular interstitium, a connective tissue sheath that surrounds the central bronchi and pulmonary arteries. The peribronchovascular interstitium extends from the level of the pulmonary hila into the peripheral lung. This feature may be ascertained on high-resolution computer tomography.
A pregnancy in which the fertilized egg inserts in a location outside of the main cavity of the uterus .

Expectoration of a broncholith. Broncholithiasis is defined as the presence of calculi in the tracheobronchial tree. It is a rare disease but can be characterized by clinical and radiological findings of a calcified lymph node eroding bronchial wall and opening into the bronchial lumen.
Abnormality of the spatial relationship of the atria to other components of the heart.
Absence or developmental hypoplasia of the uterus.
A papule with the same color as the surrounding skin.
A functional anomaly of mitochondria.
Inflammation of the sacroiliac joint, generally accompanied by lower back pain.
A function abnormality of the endocrine pancreas.
Abnormally increased size of the knee joint.
An [MASK], comprising the left nasal bone and the right nasal bone.
An anomaly of the adjacent structures of the eye, defined as the lacrimal apparatus, the extraocular muscles and the eyelids, eyelashes, eyebrows and the conjunctiva.
Anomalous anatomical placement of the eyebrow.

Structural anomaly of the fetal membranes , which comprise a vital intrauterine compartment, where they perform mechanical, immune, and endocrine functions to promote growth of the fetus and protection from environmental adversity. Amniochorionic membranes anatomically consist of a single layer of cuboidal amnion epithelial cells, chorionic trophoblasts, and scattered fibroblasts connected by a layer of type IV collagen-rich extracellular matrix.
A congenital lesion of the sclera characterized by unilateral patchy but extensive slate-gray or bluish discoloration of the sclera . The conjunctiva are spared.

Any structural anomaly of the interstitium of the kidney. The renal interstitium is defined as the intertubular, extraglomerular, extravascular space of the kidney. It is bounded on all sides by tubular and vascular basement membranes and is filled with cells, extracellular matrix, and interstitial fluid.
Displacement or malalignment of one or more joints in the lower extremity .
A general term referring to a defect in immunity resulting from impaired antibody production.
Adrenal insufficiency secondary to a defect in ACTH production.

Accessory pathway-related [MASK] involves an abnormal electrical conduction of the accessory pathway. The accessory pathway connecting impulses between the atrium and the ventricle can be seen at any site in the AV groove.
Enlargement of the chamber of the left heart ventricle.
A tumor of the heart.

Any deviation from the normal level of growth hormone in the blood circulation. GH or somatotropin is a peptide hormone that stimulates growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration. Its secretion from the pituitary is regulated by the neurosecretory nuclei of the hypothalamus, which can release Growth hormone-releasing hormone and Growth hormone-inhibiting hormone into the hypophyseal portal venous blood surrounding the pituitary. GH is secreted in a pulsatile manner, which is one of the reasons why an isolated measurement of its blood concentration is not meaningful.
A functional anomaly of the large intestine.
Increased susceptibility to streptococcus pneumoniae infections as manifested by a history of recurrent infections by streptococcus pneumoniae.
A [MASK] from its normal position .

Reduced function of the muscles required to generate subatmospheric pressure in the thoracic cavity during breathing: the diaphragm, the external intercostal and the interchondral part of the internal intercostal muscles.
A tumor of the genitourinary system.
[MASK] is a short and generally painful infection of the middle ear.
An anomaly of cerebral veins.
An increase in the thickness of the pleura, generally related to scarring of the pleural tissue.
Deposition of calcium salts in gonadal tissue.
An anomaly in platelet form, ultrastructure, or intracellular organelles.
Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the sacral bone.
Congenital absence or underdevelopment of the fovea centralis.
A type of cerebral palsy characterized by slow, involuntary muscle movement and mixed muscle tone.
A type of contracture in which the plantar flexion muscles are contracted.

A type of cancer that originates in the peritoneum. It is to be distinguished from metastatic cancer of the peritoneum. Peritoneal cancer can occur anywhere in the abdominal space, and affects the surface of organs contained inside the peritoneum.
An abnormality of an atrioventricular valve.
A tumor of the scrotum.
Swelling of the retinal nerve fibers.

An abnormality in perception of contrast. Spatial contrast is a physical dimension referring to the light-dark transition of a border or an edge in an image that delineates the existence of a pattern or an object. Contrast sensitivity refers to a measure of how much contrast a person requires to see a target. Contrast-sensitivity measurements differ from acuity measurements; acuity is a measure of the spatial-resolving ability of the visual system under conditions of very high contrast, whereas contrast sensitivity is a measure of the threshold contrast for seeing a target.
Impotence resulting from abnormal functioning of the autonomic nervous system.

Toxoplasmosis is a widespread parasitic infection that is frequently asymptomatic in immunocompetent patients. However, this obligate intracellular protozoan parasite can evade the immune system and persist for the life of its host in cyst form, predominantly in the brain, retina, and muscles. Reactivation of latent cysts may occur when the immune system fails to maintain cytokine pressure, which mainly relies on gamma interferon . Toxoplasmosis is a life-threatening infection in immunocompromised patients .
An [MASK], i.e., of the muscle on the palm of the human hand just beneath the thumb.

Inflammation of the layers of tissue that cover the brain and spinal cord and of the fluid-filled space between the meninges when it is caused by disorders that are not infections or by drugs or vaccines.

A focal seizure characterized at onset by predominantly proximal limb or axial muscles producing irregular sequential ballistic movements, such as pedaling, pelvic thrusting, thrashing, rocking movements.
An [MASK], the organ that connects the developing fetus to the uterine wall to enable nutrient uptake, waste elimination, and gas exchange.
An [MASK] tooth.
Decreased secretion of luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone by the hypothalamus.
Reduced strength of the orbicularis oculi, the circumorbital muscle in the face that closes the eyelid.
A developmental defect characterized by the abnormal fusion of the proximal tibia and fibula.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against insulin.
[MASK] occurs between menstrual periods, after sex, or after menopause. Menstrual periods that are heavier or last longer than usual or last more than seven days also are considered abnormal.
An abnormality of the outline, configuration, or contour of the mouth.
A type of focal motor seizure in which awareness is retained throughout the seizure.
An abnormality of a cardiac ventricle.

Extracellular deposition in cardiac tissue of a proteinaceous material that, when stained with Congo red, demonstrates apple-green birefringence under polarized light and that has a distinct color when stained with sulfated Alcian blue. Viewed with electron microscopy, the amyloid deposits are seen to be composed of a beta-sheet fibrillar material. These nonbranching fibrils have a diameter of 7.5 to 10 nm and are the result of protein misfolding.
A structural anomaly of nerves of the enteric nervous system.
Decrease in width of the nasal tip.
An abnormality of the structure or appearance of the umbilicus.
An abnormal increase in the thickness of a tendon.
An abnormally high increase in insulin levels following a glucagon stimulation test.
An elevation in bone density in one or more tarsal bones of the foot. Sclerosis is normally detected on a radiograph as an area of increased opacity.

Reduced activity of plasminogen activator inhibitor 1. This protein down-regulates fibrinolysis in the circulation by inhibiting the two major plasminogen activators: tissue-plasminogen activator and urokinase-plasminogen activator.
A fontanelle that is small for age.
An [MASK], i.e., of the muscles on the ulnar side of the palm of the hand .
A type of transposition of the great arteries in which aorta is in front of and primarily to the left of the pulmonary artery.
The presence of a fistula between the perineum and the rectum.
An abnormality of the sinoatrial node in the right atrium. THe SA node acts as the pacemaker of the heart.
An [MASK], an ossicle in the middle ear.

Concentration of prealbumin in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal. Prealbumin, also known as transthyretin, has a half-life in plasma of about 2 days, much shorter than that of albumin. Prealbumin is therefore more sensitive to changes in protein-energy status than albumin, and its concentration closely reflects recent dietary intake rather than overall nutritional status.
Abnormality/dysplasia of a single myeloid cell .
EEG with focal sharp transient waves of a duration less than 80 msec in the frontal region.
A clinical sign indicating a lapse of posture and is usually manifest by a bilateral flapping tremor at the wrist, metacarpophalangeal, and hip joints.
Increased width of metaphyses of the arms.

A slowly progressing leukemia characterized by a clonal proliferation of maturing and mature myeloid cells or mature lymphocytes. When the clonal cellular population is composed of myeloid cells, the process is called chronic myelogenous leukemia. When the clonal cellular population is composed of lymphocytes, it is classified as chronic lymphocytic leukemia, hairy cell leukemia, or T-cell large granular lymphocyte leukemia.
Affective, mnemonic or composite perceptual auras with subjective qualities similar to those experienced in life but are recognized by the subject as occurring outside of actual context.

Abnormal decrease of double negative CD3+CD4-CD8- T cells, measured as percentage of total CD3+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These are usually measured within the TCR alpha/beta positive population.

A type of weakness of the muscles involved in chewing that occurs after a muscle group is used and lessens if the muscle group has some rest. That is, there is diminution of strength with repetitive muscle actions.
A tumor of the eye.
A form of hemolytic anemia that occurs in repeated episodes.

Hemoglobin A contains two globin alpha chains and two globin beta chains. HbA is normally the main adult hemoglobin, representing about 96-98 percent of all hemoglobin. This term represents a decreased in the proportion of HbA below this limit, and can be seen in various forms of thalassemia.
A neoplasm originating in the pharynx.

Progressive PR interval prolongation with the subsequent occurrence of a single nonconducted P wave that results in a pause. The pause that follows the nonconducted impulse is less than fully compensatory .
Any abnormality of the morphology of the major calices or minor calices of the kidney.
A structural anomaly of the nephron.
An abnormality of the cortex of the kidney.
An [MASK], which is the inclined bony region of the posterior cranial fossa located between the sella turcica and the foramen magnum.
Displacement of the 2nd finger from its normal position.
A functional anomaly of the hepatobiliary system
An abnormal increase in the size of nasopharyngeal adenoids.

An increase of medial mucoid extracellular matrix creating translamellar and/or intralamellar expansions including extracellular pools as noted on an H&E stain and/or a stain to highlight extracellular matrix material .
Missing humerus bone associated with congenital failure of development.
Concentration of biopterin in the cerebrospinal fluid below the lower limit of normal.
Pruritus is an itch or a sensation that makes a person want to scratch. This term refers to an abnormally increased sensation of itching over the palm of the hand.

Abnormal increase or decrease of the naive CD4+ T cell subpopulation, commonly characterized as CD45RA+, CD45RO-, or CD27+, measured as percentage of total CD4+ T cells in the blood, compared to a reference range for a given sex and age-group. These cells are sometimes also characterized as CD62L+ and CCR7+.
A [MASK] is a yellowish to brown protruding lesion in the conjunctiva that is easily seen on the nasal and temporal sides of the cornea.
Aplasia or developmental hypoplasia of the tragus.
An abnormally increased level of alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme in the blood.
Abnormality of the growth of the pubic hair. Pubic hair is part of the secondary sexual hair, which normally ensues during puberty.
Any anomaly of the function of the spleen.
A glioma affecting the brainstem.
Narrowing or constriction of the inner surface of a cerebral artery.
An abnormality of the formation and mineralization of an epiphysis.
Abnormally large size of the epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers with respect to age-dependent norms.
Vitreous humor of the eye displaying beaded bundles of irregular diameters.
Reduced transparency of the central portion of the corneal stroma.
An abnormality of blood coagulation, common pathway.
Behavior that is not in line with social norms.
EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the parietal region, i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

An anomalous structural finding of the fetal gastrointestinal system. Terms in this subhierarchy are restricted to findings that can only be observed in the prenatal period. Other HPO terms can also be used to describe fetal phenotypes.
[MASK], i.e., of the almond-shaped gland that secretes the aqueous layer of the tear film for each eye.
A progressive loss of the ability to remember the meaning of words, faces and objects.
The absence of the normal curvature of the vertebral column.
An [MASK], which forms the lower and back part of the hip bone.
Unintentional movement in one area of the body produced during intentional movement of another area of the body.

A type of chest pain that arises in the or under the left breast and often described as throbbing, stabbing, or burning, and lasting hours or longer. The pain may arise with or after effort, and may spread to the left arm or left side of the neck.
Partial duplication of the third proximal phalanx of hand, seen on x-rays as a broad and/or bifid phalanx.

The carpus consists of the scaphoid, lunate, triquetal, pisiform, captitate, hamate, trapezoid, and trapezium bones. The tarsus consists of the talus, calcaneus, cuboid, cuneiform, and navicular bones. This term applies if there is any fusion among the bones of the carpus or tarsus.
A structural anomaly of the vessel that contains or conveys lymph fluid.
Inability to detect any qualitative olfactory sensation.
An [MASK], i.e., the Acetabular part of hip bone, which together with the head of the femur forms the hip joint.
An abnormal level of an analyte measured in the blood.
Abnormality of the growth of the axillary hair. Axillary hair is part of the secondary sexual hair, which normally ensues during puberty.

An anomalous response to the corticotropin releasing hormone stimulation test. Normally,CRH is released by the hypothalamus to induce adrenocorticotropic hormone release by the anterior pituitary. In the stimulation test, CRH is administered intravenously and ACTH and cortisol are measured at intervals.
Small protrusion within the pinna.
Disturbance in the atrial activation that is caused by transient failure of impulse conduction from the sinoatrial node to the cardiac atria.

A structural anomaly of the chordae tendinae of the mitral valve, whose main function is to transmit the contraction and relaxation of the papillary muscles during the cardiac cycle, thus ensuring the closing of the leaflets of the mitral valve.
An abnormal accumulation of fluid and swelling in the tongue.
[MASK], the conic projection from the posterior edge of the middle of the soft palate.
Breakage of the sclera.
A decreased amount of collagen VI in muscle tissue. Collagen VI is a primarily associated with the extracellular matrix of skeletal muscle.
Trophic changes occurring in a limb.
Nodules that form between Bruch's membrane and the retinal pigment epithelium.
Any functional anomaly of the mitral valve.
EEG with focal sharp transient waves in the frontal region, i.e., focal sharp waves of a duration less than 80 msec followed by a slow wave.

A deviation from normal range of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate , a test that measures the distance that erythrocytes have fallen after one hour in a vertical column of anticoagulated blood under the influence of gravity. The ESR is a nonspecific finding. An elevation may indicate inflammation or may be caused by any condition that elevates fibrinogen. A decreased ESR may be seen in polycythemia or in certain blood diseases in which red blood cells have an irregular or smaller shape that causes slower settling.
Any deviation from the normal concentration of C-reactive protein in the blood circulation.
Any anomaly of the anterior horn cell.
Absence or underdevelopment of the nasal septum.
Any abnormality of the proximal epiphysis of the femur.
Absence of one or more epiphyses of the phalanges of the fingers.
An abnormal flattening of an epiphysis of femur.
Developmental anomaly in which the vagina, bladder, and rectum fuse resulting in a common channel.
Any form of seizure occurring at the time of a fever without infection of the central nervous system, and without an alternative cause such as severe metabolic derangement, occurring at any age.
A buildup of fluid that causes swelling in the soft tissues of the genital area.

A fourfold or greater increase of usual seizure frequency within a 3-day period, where the patient demonstrates full recovery between seizure events within the cluster. The [MASK] should be recognizable by the primary clinician, carer or patient.
Any abnormality of the third metacarpal bone.
Hypoplasia of the maxillozygomatic complex.
An abnormal morphology of the distal phalanx of the big toe, with a short and wide phalanx that tapers distally. Bullet-shaped phalanges lack the normal diaphyseal constriction.
A [MASK] results from a tear in the rectovaginal septum . Rectal tissue bulges through this tear and into the vagina as a hernia. There are two main causes of this tear: childbirth, and hysterectomy.
Regurgitation of milk through the nose.
Abnormality in single fiber EMG recording, a technique that allows identification of action potentials from individual muscle fibers.

A band of bone material of decreased density forming alongside the surface of the cortical bone with thickening of the periosteum. Callus formation in the affected area is common and gives the appearance of a false fracture.
An arachnoid cyst located at the margin of the cerebellum and pons.
The presence of autoantibodies in the serum that react against nucleoporin 62.
Any abnormality in the relative amount of CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes.

A type of focal automatism seizure characterized by coordinated bilateral or unilateral movements of the feet or legs at onset. The movement is more reminiscent of normal movements in amplitude, and is less frenetic or rapid in comparison to the movements seen in focal hyperkinetic seizures involving the legs.
Any anomaly of the function of the endocrine system.
Radiographic features include a dilated, radiolucent lesion typically located eccentrically within the metaphyseal portion of the bone, with fluid levels visible on magnetic resonance imaging.
An abnormal dilation of the rectum. There is a large filled rectum as a result of underlying innervation or muscular abnormalities, which remains after disimpaction of the rectum.
A primitive neuroectodermal neoplasm that occurs in the central nervous system.
Increased susceptibility to enteroviral infections, as manifested by recurrent episodes of enteroviral infection.
An abnormality of the structure or composition of the teeth.
Absence or underdevelopment of the diaphragm.
Concentration of the complement component factor I in the blood circulation below the lower limit of normal.
A form of hemolytic anemia that is triggered by ingestion of certain drugs.

Pachygyria with cortical thickness above 10 mm with and a posterior predominant severity gradient. The severity gradient is determined based on the gyral width, with gyri typically wider than 5mm over the more severely affected regions. Posterior predominant gradient indicates pachygyria more severe other the occipital lobes but also includes a rare perisylvian-predominant pachygyria and a temporal predominant pachygyria.
Increased pigmentation of the scrotum.
A darker than expected T2 signal on magnetic resonance imaging of the brainstem. This term refers to a localized hypointensity affecting a particular region of the brainstem.
The presence of atheromas or atherosclerotic plaques in the aorta.

A type of blepharitis that affects the meibomian glands and meibomian gland orifices. This abnormality can be associated with a spectrum of appearances ranging from meibomian seborrhoea and meibomianitis , to chalazia.
The tPA protein catalyzes the conversion of plasiminogen to plasmin, and thus break down of clots. When there is a deficiency there will be an increase of thrombosis
Reduced level of plasminogen activator inhibitor 1 antigen.
An abnormally decreased amount of thyroxin-binding globulin in blood. TBG is responsible for carrying the thyroid hormones thyroxine and 3,5,3'-triiodothyronine in the bloodstream.
Persistence of the urachal canal with drainage of urine from the bladder through the persistent allantois canal to the umbilicus.
Gain-of-function thyroid-stimulating hormone receptor defect.
Increased passive stiffness or tightness of the neck musculature.
A lower than normal concentration of 2-oxoglutaric acid in the urine.
The concentration of methylsuccinic acid in the urine, normalized for urine concentration, is above the upper limit of normal.

An emotional state characterized by excessive, persistent, or contextually inappropriate negative inner experiences involving emotional arousal and valence. These experiences are often associated with negative perceptions of the self, the future, the past, or the surrounding environment, and may include affective bias such as interpreting neutral or ambiguous stimuli as negative. The intensity, duration, or impact of the state exceeds what would be expected for the individual based on their baseline emotional functioning, the context, cultural norms, or situational triggers, or when it persists despite efforts at self-regulation.
An increased amount of urobilinogen present in the stool.
